source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I have red spots all over the body with fever and pain behind the ears. Why?
===============================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Mashfika N Alam**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jun 23, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I am 49 years old female. I have red spots all over my body. I have pain in the thigh and back. I have a fever for the past two days. I have pain behind my ears with a headache. I am unable to eat my food. I have slight coughing and slight swelling on my face.

【9】Answered by **Dr. Mashfika N Alam**

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】It is most likely a viral fever. It is better to get a complete blood count done to be on the safer side. Have plenty of fluids and take rest. Do not take Aspirin, Ibuprofen, or any other NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) or painkillers. You can take Paracetamol three tablets a day for fever.

source_info.title: Can a single exposure to silica dust cause silicosis?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can a single exposure to silica dust cause silicosis?
========================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Chandra Shekhar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Dec 05, 2022 and last reviewed on: Jul 20, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I have a question about silica dust exposure. I have been working on a fireplace, and the surrounding had a lot of dried grout. I was sanding the grout with a metal brush. I used an N95 dust mask for protection. However, I have not realized that the grout contained silica which is very harmful to the lungs. I am worried if N95 rendered enough protection. There was a lot of dust during the sanding around me and in my hair and clothes. I took a shower later. Also, please tell me if my family members are at risk if they were in and out of that without any masks. I am afraid that my infant was also exposed. He was there for about two hours after I was done sanding, but before the cleanup, he was about 10 feet away from the fireplace. But there was enough silica dust in the air to cause him damage. Should I be concerned about silicosis?

【9】Answered by Dr. Chandra Shekhar

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com. I read your query and can understand your concern. Only with long exposure, maybe about ten years, does the risk of silicosis increase. Even with a mask, there is exposure. Advise family members to maintain a distance of 500 meters. Since it is your occupation, periodically check your respiratory health and do spirometry and high-resolution computed tomography thorax. I hope this helps.

【13】Patient's Query

【14】Hi doctor,

【15】The family members were about three to five meters away. Is this considered high exposure? I have read that it usually takes years of exposure to cause silicosis. Is one exposure like this enough to cause silicosis?

【16】Answered by Dr. Chandra Shekhar

【17】#

【18】Hi,

【19】Welcome back to icliniq.com. I read your query and can understand your concern. Yes, three to five meters distance is a high-risk zone, and you and your family using N95 is a good thing. It delays the disease development process. Periodical checks are recommended. Silicosis usually takes ten years to develop, and also when it develops, it presents as end-stage lung disease . Sanding may cause silicosis, but mainly stone cutters, mines workers and brick makers are at higher risk of silicosis . I hope this information is helpful.

【20】* * *

source_info.title: I had fever for two days with chest and throat pain. Is this COVID-19 infection?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I had fever for two days with chest and throat pain. Is this COVID-19 infection?
===================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Shubadeep Debabrata Sinha**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Vinodhini. J

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Aug 15, 2020 and last reviewed on: Sep 11, 2020_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I had a fever for two days and felt a little pain in my chest and throat with body weakness on the fourth day. Now I am eating, moving, and walking normally. I doubt it is COVID-19 because I came in contact with infected people.

【9】My question is if it is COVID-19, is it the end of it as I feel less pain? Or I may have other symptoms again?

【10】I am currently taking Paracetamol and Azithromycin.

【11】Answered by Dr. Shubadeep Debabrata Sinha

【12】#

【13】Hello,

【14】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【15】I feel sorry for your discomfort.

【16】COVID-19 causes several symptoms including those happening to you. In addition, it causes breathlessness, cough, diarrhea, loss of smell, and appetite, which is associated with a positive COVID-19 swab culture test and lung CT (computerized tomography) scan ground glass finding, which can prove its presence. Hence to know for sure, you need to get tested for at least the swab test. The symptoms may have reduced for now but it has a tendency to revisit by 7 to 10th day.

【17】In addition to the test, I recommend you do the following.

【18】1\. Steam inhalation thrice daily.

【19】2\. Salt water gargles twice daily.

【20】3\. Diet with rich proteins (meat, lentils, beans, soybeans, milk) and citrus fruits (sweet lime, lemon, orange, etc.).

【21】4\. Take a tablet of Zinc 50 mg one tablet twice daily for 15 days, Vitamin C 500 mg one tablet twice daily for 15 days, and Vitamin D3 60K units one capsule once a week for four weeks.

【22】Please look out for an increase in current symptoms and breathlessness. Please revert after the test and take medicines in the next four to five days.

【23】* * *

source_info.title: Can you clarify the term effaced lymphoid tissue in my pathology report?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can you clarify the term effaced lymphoid tissue in my pathology report?
===========================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Prakash. H. M.**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. K Shobana

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Aug 09, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I had an open cervical lymph node biopsy performed about two months ago. They developed suddenly and became quite large over three months. I additionally have lost 35% body weight in a year. I feel incredibly fatigued, unable to eat, developed an enlarged spleen and even showed a sharp drop in my blood counts. The surgeon, who performed the biopsy, indicated that the pathology report was normal. But, after learning that he caused debilitating damage to my spinal accessory nerve, I would like to get a second opinion of the report. Here is what it says. Diagnosis: Skeletal muscle, fibroconnective and fibroadipose tissue with somewhat effaced, but lymphoid tissue with extensive crush artifact. Note: Impacted foreign material is also identified. The process appears to be reactive in nature; however extensive crush artifact is present thereby limiting interpretation. Please correlate with clinical findings. Was there an antecedent procedure at the site? Gross description - Specimen consists of two irregular fragments of tan tissue measuring 1.2 x 1.0 x 0.5 and 1.0 x 0.4 x 0.3. The largest piece has white sutures attached, which are removed. The specimen is entirely submitted in one cassette. The surgeon assured me two months ago that everything looked great and allowed me to read the report. Can you clarify the terms effaced lymphoid tissue, impacted foreign material and irregular fragments? Also, in what condition they are commonly seen? What process appears to be reactive in nature? Does the gross description indicate two pieces of lymphoid tissue or two complete lymph nodes? I was told that he removed four complete nodes. Should he have submitted all four? The measurements do not indicate which unit of measurement was used, but do the numbers seem normal? Is there any reason for sutures have been attached to the largest piece of tissue? Please explain.

【9】Answered by Dr. Prakash. H. M.

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Based on your query, my opinion is as follows. When the nodes are small, during biopsy due to holding by forceps to remove the nodes, crush artifacts are known to occur. Larger nodes are much easier to remove without crush artifacts, whereas in smaller nodes, it can occur. To be more precise, it can occur more in normal, because abnormal lymph nodes are usually firm to hard. Normal nodes are known to be soft in nature and more commonly crush artifacts can be found, if the node is small. Effaced lymphoid tissue means the structure of a lymph node is a bit altered. Reactive means, more lymphoid follicles are present, indicating the lymph node response to infection. Impacted foreign material, here the suture is the foreign material. Sometimes to identify nodes or tissues, it is common to suture the tissue. As multiple nodes were removed, to identify the initial node, it is often tagged. As no pathology was found, it has no significance. Sometimes, the nodes will be small and stick to each other during processing. Hence, instead of four nodes, they might have found two larger nodes. The measurement is usually in centimeters, means it is very small. Irregular fragments, means the tissue while removing, as they are soft in nature, loose the nodular shape. Hence, they are termed irregular fragments. Based on the size and part of tissue showing reactive nature, I would not suspect anything wrong in the pathology report. If the nodes were larger or at present if you have any large and hard nodes, then further evaluation will be necessary.

【14】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can I complete my rabies vaccination course or restart it as I was bitten again?
===================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Arpit Varshney**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Mar 15, 2022 and last reviewed on: Jul 14, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am currently on a course of rabies vaccination (post-exposure prophylaxis, category 2). Last month, I got my third dose and got bitten by my dog again on my feet. My next dose will be next week, and I cannot go or ask the doctor at the moment. It was not a bite, but it got my skin broken. I washed the wound with soap and water quickly and used Povidone-iodine. I do not have any symptoms. My dog is just two months old and does not have an anti-rabies vaccine. I observed him for two weeks, and there was nothing unusual. I would like to ask if I have to continue with my fourth dose, or do I still need to go through another course of vaccination or booster?

【9】Answered by Dr. Arpit Varshney

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I understand your concern. Once you have received the rabies vaccine full dose, it is effective for the next five years. There is no need to repeat the vaccine even if you are bit by a dog again. Your previous vaccine is good enough. They will save you from rabies. So, for now, complete your vaccination course as it is going on. No need to restart the course again. You will not acquire rabies because your puppy is a pet, young, and never exposed to rabid dogs. Also, your injury is minimal. So stay tension-free. You are going to be fine. Hope this helps. Kindly revert in case of further queries. Thank you.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: Can HLA-B27 positivity and my ear pain be related?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can HLA-B27 positivity and my ear pain be related?
=====================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Srivastava Durgesh**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Dec 01, 2022 and last reviewed on: Jul 21, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I am a 25-year-old female. For the last two months, I have had some pains in the right ear (back side) and neck. I went for some tests, and I came to know that HLA-B27 is positive. I am currently working and cannot concentrate as I get severe pain. I have a few questions regarding HLA-B27. 1. Why HLA-B27 is positive? Is it because of any deficiency in the body? 2. What is the reason for HLA-B27 is positive? Will I face any problems in the future after marriage? The medicine which I am using currently is Naproxen. Also, the doctor asked me to use eye drops for one month.

【9】Answered by Dr. Srivastava Durgesh

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I understand your concern. Please answer the following questions to know further details.

【14】1.  Did you have any redness in your eye, also? (the reason for eye drops).
2.  Do you have pain in the back, also?
3.  Is your neck pain worst in the morning time?

【15】HLA (human leukocyte antigens) B27 is an immunological marker of a group of rheumatological diseases called spondyloarthritis. It is a gene that is present by birth. So it is positive because it came from your parents. HLA B27 may be present in about 7 % of people, but the disease occurs in only a few. So it is significant only if your symptoms correlate with those of spondyloarthritis . It does not directly affect pregnancy or childbearing. Naproxen alone may not be helpful. You may contact a rheumatologist there or may contact me for any further queries. I hope it was helpful.

【16】Thank you.

【17】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. How can a skinny person gain weight and stay healthy?
========================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Suneetha B S**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Feb 03, 2023 and last reviewed on: Jul 18, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am concerned about my weight. I am skinny and eat a lot, but I still do not gain weight. Kindly help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Suneetha B S

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】To gain weight healthily, you need to build muscle, and I advise you to indulge in regular physical activity and a healthy diet. Healthy diet: Do not start eating oily or junk food to gain weight, because that would only lead to a gain in fat but health problems, like high cholesterol and heart disease . For a healthy diet, increase your protein intake in the form of sprouts, nuts, egg white, and lean meats like fish and chicken. Follow up your workouts by drinking a whey protein supplement within ten minutes of completing your workout. Then, divide it into small meals every two hours instead of three main meals daily. That makes it eight to twelve small meals in a day. Physical exercise **:** If you are above 17 years of age, you can start by joining the gym. Do ten minutes of cardio followed by strength training. Start by lifting lighter weights. Listen to your body, and slowly move on to heavier weights when it allows you. You can hire a qualified trainer to help you get results faster and guide you to do your exercises correctly. Improper posture and breathing patterns during exercise can lead to injury. Before you start any exercise program, visit a doctor for a proper physical examination to understand if the exercise suits you and to prevent injury. A good eight hours of sleep and eating meals right on time are very important. I hope that helps. Thank you.

【9】Answered by Dr. Suneetha B S

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

source_info.title: My mother is diabetic as well as hypertensive. Please give an opinion on her retinal detachment.
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. My mother is diabetic as well as hypertensive. Please give an opinion on her retinal detachment.
===================================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Hussein Mohamed Sherif Ahmed Ayoub**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Vinodhini. J

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 28, 2020 and last reviewed on: Jul 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am worried about my mother's retinal detachment. She has diabetes and hypertension. I have an x-ray of her eye. She is currently located abroad and I would love to have a second opinion on what process she should be taking.

【9】Answered by Dr. Hussein Mohamed Sherif Ahmed Ayoub

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Let me first reassure you, your mother case seems to be not urgent. Judging by the information you gave and the attached O.C.T scan _(attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ) you have done. The left eye seems quite normal. The right eye has some macular edema. Meaning that there is fluid in the retina that is causing retinal stretching. Also, I can see neurosensory detachment in the retina too, this is probably due to long-standing diabetes. Retinal detachment usually manifests with seeing a bright light and floaters in the visual field as well as a drop of vision. (I will need to know if anything new happened to her vision). In this case, my opinion is, your ophthalmologist will need to Intravitreal injections of Avastin. This will help absorb the fluid leaking in the retina and causing the stretching. If there is detachment he will need to reposition the retina with a vitrectomy procedure and retinal fixation and implanting temporary silicone. Do not worry this procedure can help maintain vision and maybe fix it for the better. It can be a little bit costly and you have to select an experienced vitreoretinal surgeon.Diabetes control, your mom will need to check her diabetes with an internist. I need to know further information as regards to her vision, previous medical history and operation done. When was the last time she has checked with an ophthalmologist so I can help you and tell you more about her management.

【14】* * *

【15】**Differential diagnosis:**  

【16】Retinal degeneration.

【17】**Probable diagnosis:**  

【18】Macular edema. Neurosensory detachment.

【19】* * *

source_info.title: What is the reason for recurring white spots on my genital area?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What is the reason for recurring white spots on my genital area?
===================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Muhammad Majid Hanif**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jan 03, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I have had **white spots on my genital area for the past one year** . They are not bumps but just spots. They do not itch or smell. They are only just visible. After applying a cream such as Beclomin for prolonged periods, it goes away but once I stop, it starts to appear again.

【9】Answered by Dr. Muhammad Majid Hanif

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】This seems to be related to some **atypical skin lesions that respond well to Beclomin ( Beclomethasone and Miconazole nitrate)** ( _attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ). These can or cannot be sexually transmitted disease-related symptoms. It depends on proper evaluation and testing to rule out the real cause. In differential diagnosis, **lichen sclerosis** can be on top. In this disease, we see patchy white lesions on male genitalia. Skin diseases like lichen planus and psoriasis can be other differentials.

【14】The best next step is to consult a dermatologist in-person to get yourself tested thoroughly. The dermatologist would rule out all possible causes including fungal infections and aforementioned possibilities. Once diagnosed properly, it can be managed accordingly.

【15】For more information consult an **internal medicine physician online** \--> https://www.icliniq.com/ask-a-doctor-online/internal-medicine-physician

【16】Patient's Query

【17】Thank you doctor,

【18】Kindly tell me whether it is fine for me to have unprotected sex with my wife or not. Can this get cured entirely or not?

【19】Answered by Dr. Muhammad Majid Hanif

【20】#

【21】Hi,

【22】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【23】The answer to both of your queries is that **it depends on the original diagnosis** . If it comes up not to be communicable, you are good to go unprotected. Otherwise, better to go protected.

【24】As far as treatment and cure are concerned, it also depends on the diagnosis. Better is to **go for the consultation from a dermatologist** . It would be the best next step.

【25】For more information consult an **internal medicine physician online** \--> https://www.icliniq.com/ask-a-doctor-online/internal-medicine-physician

【26】* * *

source_info.title: How can the feeling of pressure inside the ear be relieved?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. How can the feeling of pressure inside the ear be relieved?
==============================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Shyam Kalyan. N**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Divya Banu M

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am a 21-year-old female and 160 pounds and at a height of 5’6". I have been having a problem with my left ear. I woke up one morning and felt that it was clogged and made the mistake of using a Q-tip which resulted in my being unable to pop my ear. That was over a week ago. I have tried wax softener drops and a saline spray to try and clean my ears out but it has not worked. Now there is a pressure inside my ear. I am not sure what to do. Is there anything I can do to fix this?

【9】Answered by Dr. Shyam Kalyan. N

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Possibilities are impacted wax, ear canal infection, middle ear infection, eustachian tube catarrh. Unless one sees inside the ear using an otoscope or endoscope it is difficult to diagnose. However, a course of antibiotic with decongestant and keeping ears dry till you get better can work in an empirical way for most of the diagnoses listed above. If you need more information on that revert back to me. One can buy ear cameras and they do help in cases like yours where you are not able to go to an ENT. You can take pictures of the inside of the ear and share with us online and we can guide you on what is to be done.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: Is there a way to cover keloid on chest to avoid rubbing and irritation?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Is there a way to cover keloid on chest to avoid rubbing and irritation?
===========================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. G. S. S. Sandeep**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Sep 02, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 27, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I have had a keloid I guess at the center of my chest for the past year and a new one developed a few months back. I took treatment but was not effective. I used to take Isotretinoin capsules daily and apply Clobkare cream. One major problem I face with them is they rub against the shirt and irritate especially the new one. Is there a tape or something I can apply to them while exercising and going out because I also have hair in that area?

【9】Answered by Dr. G. S. S. Sandeep

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Keloids are a type of scar that itches or irritates when something touches it. Do not apply any tapes or plaster because if you try to remove the tape you will pluck your hair which in turn induces keloid formation. You can plan for intralesional Triamcinolone injection along with cryotherapy this will help in reducing keloid.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor,

【16】Is there something I can use there which will reduce friction with the clothes because it really irritates when I walk?

【17】Answered by Dr. G. S. S. Sandeep

【18】#

【19】Hi,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】You can apply Calamine lotion whenever it irritates or you can try Melipox (Aloe vera, Oatmeal, etc.) spray if it is available at your place. You can spray as on required. You can apply Vaseline on the chest prior to gauze bandage. This will prevent hair follicles from plucking when you try to remove the bandage. Avoid hair follicle trauma.

【22】* * *

source_info.title: Is there any way to reduce ketone levels in a diabetic patient?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Is there any way to reduce ketone levels in a diabetic patient?
==================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Prabhakar Laxman Jathar**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Divya Banu M

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 10, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am a diabetes patient. My sugar level in fasting is above 350 mg/dL and I checked ketone in urine, it was found to be 4+. My height is 5' 5" approximately and weight is 136 pounds. What can I do for ketone?

【9】Answered by Dr. Prabhakar Laxman Jathar

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Ketones usually develop more often in T1 diabetes. Especially when there is no adequate insulin and glucose levels are higher than 300 to 350 mg. It is necessary to take adequate water to eliminate those through urine. Avoid exercise when ketones are present. Try and maintain closer to normal glucose levels. Check glucose levels at home more often (every 3 to 4 hours). There is no mention of what is the treatment with the dosage of various drugs, PP glucose level, and HbA1c %. You have to bring glucose in better control to prevent ketones developing. If proper care is not taken, there can be a further complication of developing diabetic ketoacidosis, a medical emergency. If you have any questions please do come back. Plus it is necessary to look at your current treatment (drugs and dosage), diet pattern and extent of daily exercises.

【14】* * *

【1】Q. What are the ways to get rid of bloating, abdominal pain, or discomfort associated with acute gastroenteritis?
=================================================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Goswami Parth Rajendragiri**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Feb 07, 2023 and last reviewed on: Jul 06, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I had some chinese food from a place I had never eaten previously for lunch. I was fine. Later that night, I ate crab legs around 11 pm. I stood up for a while and then went to sleep. I woke up at 5 am the next day feeling queasy and bloated, and my stomach was hurting. I went upstairs to use the bathroom and moved my bowels. After, I stood up for a while and drank some water. Next, my stomach started to hurt again, and I had to move my bowels again. I used the bathroom about four times that morning. I eventually went back to sleep, but when I woke up to get ready for work, I was feeling queasy. I still went to work and ate something light for lunch, like soup, but I still felt queasy. My stomach is not hurting at this point. For the next few days, I feel discomfort in my stomach, but as each day passes, it felt better than the day before. However, I still feel something slightly whenever I eat. It is going to pass eventually, but I am not sure. When I was younger, I had food poisoning that lasted for a few days with the same symptoms. Please advice.

【9】Answered by Dr. Goswami Parth Rajendragiri

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to the icliniq.com.

【13】I will help to guide you further regarding your complaint. According to history, it is a case of food poisoning that is acute gastroenteritis. Here infection might not be resolved completely, so pain can be there. It is advisable to investigate with stool routine micro examination to check pus cells, bacteria, parasite egg, etc., if present. I suggest you take an antibiotic course of Ofloxacin and Ornidazole for five days. Drink lots of water. Viral Zithromax ( Azithromycin ) powder with water can be taken for three to four days to replenish lost electrolytes. Avoid excess spicy foods. Antacids like Rabeprazole 20 mg once daily for five days can be taken. A probiotic tablet containing Lactobacillus can be taken for a week. Consult a specialist doctor, discuss with them, and take medications with their consent.

【14】Kindly follow up for further assistance. Feel free to ask further if required.

【15】Thank you.

【16】* * *

source_info.title: What do dead skin and a small scab near the genitals with no pain and itching indicate?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What do dead skin and a small scab near the genitals with no pain and itching indicate?
==========================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Dilip Kumar Meena**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 13, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】This was the first time I discovered that there was dead skin and a very small scab near my genitals. I do not know what was there before this happened but, there was no pain, itching, etc. And a few weeks later, I found these lesions again. It was the same. What is this? The last photos were taken under a microscope at home.

【9】Answered by Dr. Dilip Kumar Meena

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I understand your concern. As the lesions are subsiding, it is difficult to tell what they would have been. Right now it looks like there would have been a superficial erosion, which is healing (attachment removed to protect the patient's identity). It can be due to some primary lesion or secondary to scratching. If it happened at the same time as before, herpes genitalis can be one of the differentials but the absence of pain goes against it or it can be very mild. Have you been sexually active? If yes you can get your herpes 1 and 2 serology done to rule out herpes .

【14】Thank you.

【15】Patient's Query

【16】Hello doctor,

【17】I always check my genitals. I do not know exactly what the previous lesion was, but it must have been a similar type of lesion from the beginning. What do you mean, herpes is most likely? If not herpes, what would it be? I am worried.

【18】Answered by Dr. Dilip Kumar Meena

【19】#

【20】Hello,

【21】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【22】I understand your concern. I did not say herpes is the most likely cause, but it is one of the possibilities, that need to be considered when one is sexually active and has superficial erosions, ulcers, or vesicles at the same site over the genitals. It can be simply an excoriation, but that would be unlikely if you have no itching. It could simply be some frictional erosion due to sexual activity or maturation. If not these scenarios, you can have your herpes serology, just to rule it out. I am not labeling you as a herpes genitalis patient, without the serology. It is just one of the likely differentials along with frictional or just a scratch. In any case, with lesions over the genitals in a sexually active person, which cannot be explained by any other reason, getting an HSV (herpes simplex virus) and HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) serology is a part of routine screening. Do not get worried about it.

【23】Thank you.

【24】* * *

【1】Q. What does a semen analysis report indicate?
==============================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Vaibhav Vishal**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 24, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I and my wife have undergone many laboratory investigations as we are trying to become parents for the past four months. My grandfather has four children and my father has two so I do not think of infertility issues in the family. My wife's blood test and ultrasound reports are normal. I got my scrotum ultrasound and hormone test done and have attached the report. I want to understand the ultrasound report and what could have affected the fertility.

【9】I would like to know if my ultrasound report shows any cyst or if there is a chance of blockage in vas deference. My volume is four to five ml and I am yet to get semen analysis done. What can be expected in my semen analysis based on ultrasound and hormone levels?

【10】I have consulted an urologist and was said that there is no requirement for treatment as of now as no varicocele or cyst is present.

【11】I am in perfect health condition and my BMI is 22 and I am not overweight, I walk roughly 7000 steps a day. I eat a healthy diet like fruits (blueberry, strawberries, brazil nuts, bananas (daily), oranges) every four days a week and vegetables like kale, spinach, carrots, muli, etc. I am also taking a multivitamin, L carnitine, and CoQ 10 along with ashwagandha supplements for the past three months.

【12】I am concerned about the semen analysis test and any blockages in the tubes. I am also worried about the chromosome Y genetic defect. What can be expected in the reports and how do I proceed?

【13】Kindly help.

【14】Answered by Dr. Vaibhav Vishal

【15】#

【16】Hello,

【17】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【18】Kindly follow the suggestions already mentioned and regarding the Y chromosome defect, I would like to add that genetic testing is only required if semen analysis has any major abnormalities.

【19】I hope this has helped you.

【20】Thank you.

【21】Patient's Query

【22】Hello doctor,

【23】Thank you for the reply.

【24】I am done with the analysis, waiting for the results very anxiously now. We have been trying for four months, so timing is not an issue, only thing I am concerned is about my semen parameters which are not right. My wife went through a TV ultrasound and no HSG for tubes yet, blood tests are all normal. I am not sure what could be expected from the test as my hormones and ultrasound are normal.

【25】I want to understand if my reports, which show the following values RT valve 0.25 cm, which is 2.5 before that its 1.8 mm or 0.18 cm, are considered as grade 1 varicocele and that impacts motility or count?

【26】I am worried about the Y chromosome as it is the only thing I can doubt because the hormones and ultrasound reports are normal.

【27】Even the urologist detected no varicocele or cyst. But, what could cause the changes in levels?

【28】Kindly suggest.

【29】Answered by Dr. Vaibhav Vishal

【30】#

【31】Hello,

【32】Glad to have you back!

【33】I am here to help you get the best medical advice.

【34】I agree with your urologist that varicocele of grade 1 does notrequire treatment.

【35】I suggest you not be anxious and not worry about chromosome abnormalities at present. Wait for the semen analysis report. According to the report, further investigations or treatment, if needed, can be planned.

【36】I hope this has helped you.

【37】Thank you.

【38】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can I use emergency contraceptives to overcome withdrawal bleeding and anxiety related to irregular periods?
===============================================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Raveendran S. R**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 21, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I inquired last month about the source of my vaginal bleeding, and the doctor stated it was withdrawal bleeding. I started using I-pills around five months ago, however, there was no change in the frequency or regularity of my cycles. But recently, after getting my period taking an antidepressant resulted in withdrawal bleeding. I have been worrying a lot about my untimely periods, recently, after my period, taking an antidepressant.I took three pregnancy tests, each one week, to see if I was pregnant or not, but everything was normal. Also, my weight has suddenly increased, which is odd. Moreover, the face and legs have some sourness. Kindly help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Raveendran S. R

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I read your query and can understand your concern.

【14】Reduce your I-pill ( Levonorgestrel ) intake and make plans for alternative forms of contraception. There is no need to worry about pregnancy because you took the I-pill. There might be an infection if there is a white discharge. Schedule an abdominal ultrasound because PCOS ( Polycystic ovary syndrome ) may be the cause. Anemia may be the cause so look for hemoglobin levels. Check for folic acid, vitamin B, and vitamin D insufficiency, as it may be the cause. It might also be due to dehydration, so drink plenty of water. For the time being, you can take Livogen (folic acid and ferrous fumarate) once a night and wait for the investigation to be completed so that we can prepare for treatment.

【15】I hope this helps.

【16】Thank you and take care.

【17】Patient's Query

【18】Sir i am really sorry but you have to explain me something about my period cycle or guide me with emergency precautions or test  
  
Or should i go visit physical doc  
  
But u haven’t explained anything  
  
I hope when you reply that could really help me and release my tension

【19】Answered by Dr. Raveendran S. R

【20】\# Hi  
  
I have explained multiple reasons for the issue and the tests that need to be taken for each issue separately.  
  
cause for the period cycle - due to medication ( ipill) or other reasons which need to be investigated - test names mentioned,  
  
only in case of bleeding its emergency - Investigate to know the cause for the issue  
  
if you have pain / bleeding need to see dr in person  
  
  
  
I'm sorry you are tense - since we are not meeting in person and have not examined the patient in person I need to think of multiple diagnoses unless I have adequate reports

【21】* * *

source_info.title: Should I get a bone marrow biopsy to rule out possible MPN?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Should I get a bone marrow biopsy to rule out possible MPN?
==============================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Matías Rojas**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 12, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 21, 2022_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I am a 49-year-old female who has chronic health problems going back for awhile. Originally, I was told I had lupus but now I am beginning to think it is something else. Nine months back, I consulted an orthopedic surgeon due to suspected necrosis in left hip, after an arthrogram was done it revealed I had severe bone marrow inflammation in my si joint and was referred for a diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis, that brings me to now. **I have severe hip and leg pain, it aches constantly, severe fatigue and itching, bad headaches and migraines** . I just feel like crap and I am not getting any better. I am on Plaquenil 200 mg daily, Duloxetine 60 mg, Monica, Dexamethasone as needed, usually three days a month, Oxycodone 30 mg as needed, Imitrex as needed. Not sure how to post a copy of my lab but my RBC is 5.3 but my MCH is low 26.9, my hematocrit is 44.2. My hs-CRP is high at 6.6. My calcium and protein are both borderline high. **My ALT and bilirubin are also high** . My UA shows high for ketones, WBC, leukocyte, esters and hyaline cast. I tested negative on the HLA-B27 DNA test. My sed rate was borderline high at 19, I was negative for Sjogren's antibody as well as sm and sm/RIP antibodies. At this point, I am not sure what is going on. **Should I push for a bone marrow biopsy to rule out a possible MPN** ? I desperately want answers as to why I am in such pain and ill health.

【9】Answered by Dr. Matías Rojas

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I have checked your blood tests ( _attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ) and read your complaints about your health. **Apparently, you have a rheumatic disease** . It does not seem to be lupus or rheumatoid arthritis at first sight according to the laboratory reports. In the MRI of the hip, it actually seems to be better than the last time. I saw that **you may have a urinary tract infection according to the urinalysis you provided** (do you have a burning sensation during urination). You should follow up with a rheumatologist to further characterize your pain. Regarding pruritus, there is some test that should be done. A sonogram of your liver and some laboratory reports as well to rule out hepatic disease, blood disorders, parasitic infections in your bowels, etc. You should also get an MRI of your brain and cervical spine for a better understanding of your headache.

【14】For more information consult an **internal medicine physician online** \--> https://www.icliniq.com/ask-a-doctor-online/internal-medicine-physician

【15】* * *

【16】* * *

I am on Plaquenil 200 mg daily, Duloxetine 60 mg, Monica, Dexamethasone as needed, usually three days a month, Oxycodone 30 mg as needed, Imitrex as needed. source_info.title: Can a small thin-walled hemorrhagic cyst turn cancerous?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can a small thin-walled hemorrhagic cyst turn cancerous?
===========================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Uzma Arqam**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 11, 2018 and last reviewed on: Nov 24, 2022_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My mother is 48 years old presented with symptoms of vomiting, acidity, bloating, and headache. She is in a perimenopausal phase. She visited a gynecologist and went for a pelvic ultrasound. The reports show that she is having a small thin-walled hemorrhagic cyst with internal echoes in her right ovary and few sub centimetric nabothian cysts in her cervix. I am a bit worried if this hemorrhagic cyst is something to complex and could it turn out to be something cancerous? I am very much worried.

【9】Thank you.

【10】Answered by Dr. Uzma Arqam

【11】#

【12】Hi,

【13】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【14】I have seen your attached report ( _attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ). It would be better for me to have your mother's obstetrics, gynecological, medical, surgical and drug present and past history as I could be able to correlate symptoms. If she has been treated for any problem better to have a check on that and take regular treatment like diabetes, hypertension, etc. This perimenopausal age is very much prone to get disease due to aging. Mostly mood variations, night sweats, bone pains, all these symptoms near menopause. A woman should start taking extra care in advance near 40 years of age like calcium with vitamin D supplements, daily light exercise and walk, etc.

【15】Ovarian cyst multiloculated 2 inches or more without symptoms should have regular follow up ultrasound along with tumor marker investigations, etc., and an ovarian cyst with symptoms less than 1 to 2 inches even should be investigated. As medical and related drug history I do not know cyst with symptoms better to investigate with serum calcium 125 (antigenic tumor marker) and grey scale sonography. International multicentre research showed that cyst of 1 to 2 inches asymptomatic with normal calcium 125 have 0 % chances of malignancy. So, it is better to have serum calcium 125 done for her. Calcium 125 more than 65 units/ml has greater chances of malignancy. The hemorrhagic cyst should resolve by itself may be with minor pain. Observe for any abnormal symptoms like severe abdominal pain, abnormal bleeding report to the tertiary care center. It is better to have serum calcium 125 test and discuss here or with the local gynecologist. I hope things will be better. She should take care of all other physical problem nicely as diabetes, hypertension as many problems together also give complicated effects.

【16】Thank you.

【17】* * *

【18】* * *

source_info.title: My husband's heart rate goes up to 200 bpm after vigorous exercise. Is this ventricular ectopy?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. My husband's heart rate goes up to 200 bpm after vigorous exercise. Is this ventricular ectopy?
==================================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Ilir Sharka**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Vinodhini. J

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Oct 09, 2020 and last reviewed on: Jun 29, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My husband is 48 years old. He is in good physical shape and healthy, exercises regularly, and takes a healthy diet. During exercise, his heart rate gets to 200 bpm when at maximum exertion, which felt slightly high for his age. In mentioning this to his GP, she suggested a stress test to rule out issues. His medical history and labs are mostly great from a year ago. His last cholesterol panel was normal, and his last homocysteine was 10.5, and his inflammation markers were low. After the stress test (which I was present for and recorded), the cardiologist commented as below: You have excellent exercise performance. You had some extra beats when starting and ending, but these disappeared when exercise level increased, which is a good sign. These are benign in 95% of cases, but we should do an echo to rule out issues. After exercise ended and you were winding down, there was an abnormality as well. These could be from blockages, but the overall pattern does not support this. So it is usually due to bridging, which is your heart muscle squeezing on an artery that is relatively benign. We should do another test to check. After leaving the appointment, his doctor then provided the actual written report (attached below) and has suggested an echo and a CT angiogram. My questions are, can you have a look at the report provided and give your assessment? What is frequent ventricular ectopy at an early stage and recovery? Is this common and most likely benign? What are prolonged ST depression in the inferior and lateral leads in recovery? What could be causing this? Could it be a completely benign finding? Is the CT angiogram truly necessary? I am concerned about the excessive radiation in his chest area and wonder if there are other options here?

【9】Answered by Dr. Ilir Sharka

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I passed carefully through your husband's medical history and uploaded the test _(attachment removed to protect patient identity)_ and would explain that his test is suspicious of potential ischemic cardiac disorder. In this regard, further clinical investigations are necessary. Frequent ectopic beats ( extrasystoles ) and ST depressions on the exercise ECG (electrocardiography) may be an expression of cardiac ischemia. In order to clarify this issue, the recommended tests should be performed. You are right about CT (computed tomography) angiogram and radiation. Another rationale alternative (safe without radiation) would be stress cardiac magnetic resonance imagine test. You should discuss with your doctor about the above-mentioned issues.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor

【16】Could there be benign explanations for these issues as well? And what is the difference in the dye injected between the CT angiogram and the MRI? Would they use the same dye in both instances, so the only difference is CT (which has radiation) and MRI (no radiation)? If it is the same dye, we would definitely want to go with an MRI, but are there any clinical downsides to the MRI? Is this less accurate?

【17】Answered by Dr. Ilir Sharka

【18】#

【19】Hello,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】Contrast agents are different between CT and MRI (iodinated vs. gadolinium-based agents, respectively). MRI contrast agents are safe with very minimal potential adverse effects. I would explain that it has very high sensitivity and specificity for detecting cardiac ischemia regarding stress cardiac MRI accuracy. Only SPECT (Single-photon emission computed tomography) could be almost comparable with that. The other tests, including CT angiogram, are inferior. I would highly recommend this test.

【22】* * *

【1】Q. My husband's heart rate goes up to 200 bpm after vigorous exercise. Is this ventricular ectopy?
==================================================================================================

<mark>【2】Answered by

【3】Dr. Ilir Sharka

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Vinodhini. J

【5】This is a premium question & answer published on Oct 09, 2020 and last reviewed on: Jun 29, 2023

【6】Patient’s Query</mark>nt's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My husband is 48 years old. He is in good physical shape and healthy, exercises regularly, and takes a healthy diet. During exercise, his heart rate gets to 200 bpm when at maximum exertion, which felt slightly high for his age. In mentioning this to his GP, she suggested a stress test to rule out issues. His medical history and labs are mostly great from a year ago. His last cholesterol panel was normal, and his last homocysteine was 10.5, and his inflammation markers were low. After the stress test (which I was present for and recorded), the cardiologist commented as below: You have excellent exercise performance. You had some extra beats when starting and ending, but these disappeared when exercise level increased, which is a good sign. These are benign in 95% of cases, but we should do an echo to rule out issues. After exercise ended and you were winding down, there was an abnormality as well. These could be from blockages, but the overall pattern does not support this. So it is usually due to bridging, which is your heart muscle squeezing on an artery that is relatively benign. We should do another test to check. After leaving the appointment, his doctor then provided the actual written report (attached below) and has suggested an echo and a CT angiogram. My questions are, can you have a look at the report provided and give your assessment? What is frequent ventricular ectopy at an early stage and recovery? Is this common and most likely benign? What are prolonged ST depression in the inferior and lateral leads in recovery? What could be causing this? Could it be a completely benign finding? Is the CT angiogram truly necessary? I am concerned about the excessive radiation in his chest area and wonder if there are other options here?

<mark>【9】Answered by Dr. Ilir Sharka

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.</mark>

【13】I passed carefully through your husband's medical history and uploaded the test _(attachment removed to protect patient identity)_ and would explain that his test is suspicious of potential ischemic cardiac disorder. In this regard, further clinical investigations are necessary. Frequent ectopic beats ( extrasystoles ) and ST depressions on the exercise ECG (electrocardiography) may be an expression of cardiac ischemia. In order to clarify this issue, the recommended tests should be performed. You are right about CT (computed tomography) angiogram and radiation. Another rationale alternative (safe without radiation) would be stress cardiac magnetic resonance imagine test. You should discuss with your doctor about the above-mentioned issues.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor

【16】Could there be benign explanations for these issues as well? And what is the difference in the dye injected between the CT angiogram and the MRI? Would they use the same dye in both instances, so the only difference is CT (which has radiation) and MRI (no radiation)? If it is the same dye, we would definitely want to go with an MRI, but are there any clinical downsides to the MRI? Is this less accurate?

【17】Answered by Dr. Ilir Sharka

【18】#

【19】Hello,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】Contrast agents are different between CT and MRI (iodinated vs. gadolinium-based agents, respectively). MRI contrast agents are safe with very minimal potential adverse effects. I would explain that it has very high sensitivity and specificity for detecting cardiac ischemia regarding stress cardiac MRI accuracy. Only SPECT (Single-photon emission computed tomography) could be almost comparable with that. The other tests, including CT angiogram, are inferior. I would highly recommend this test.

【22】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What are the signs and symptoms of chronic OCD?
==================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Vishal Anilkumar Gandhi**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 15, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am 19 years old I have OCD for the last 3 years and my condition is getting worse. I am always in a low and irritated mood and always have problems understanding things interpreting everything with the wrong meaning, intrusive doubtful thoughts all the time, sleep problems, high heartbeat, problems in breathing, restlessness, suicidal thoughts, and feelings of worthless and useless, weight loss, dull skin tone since that 3 months.

【9】Kindly help.

【10】Answered by Dr. Vishal Anilkumar Gandhi

【11】#

【12】Hello,

【13】We are elated to have you onboard at icliniq.com.

【14】We understand your concerns and will help you get the best medical opinion.

【15】Thank you for taking help from a psychiatrist. I read your case and I can understand your situation. It is difficult to deal with OCD (obsessive-compulsive disorder). You are on one of the best medications for OCD but you can ask your doctor to add a capsule of Fluoxetine 20 mg daily in the morning after breakfast. You should also try to follow the below lifestyle to deal with your problem.

【16】1.  You should do exercises daily for 30 to 45 minutes like at least going for a walk.
2.  You should do meditation for 20 minutes daily, just sit in one place in a comfortable position and try to concentrate on your normal breathing, do not stop or force yourself to stop your thoughts, just let it be. It will help you to relax and reduces thoughts.
3.  You should eat healthy home-cooked foods, and avoid junk foods.
4.  You must drink enough water.
5.  You should spend quality time with friends and family daily or do video calls if you are living away from your family.
6.  You should spend time on creative hobbies like reading good books, writing journals, painting, drawing, and learning new skills or language or musical instruments.
7.  You should take enough 7 to 8 hours of sleep daily.
8.  You must avoid tobacco or alcohol or any substance abuse.
9.  Live your life, do not just spend it. Be bold and confident.
10.  Suicide is not the solution to any problem but every problem has one good solution.
11.  You must do the following blood reports as if it is not normal then it may also affect your mental illness.

【17】I hope this has helped you. Thank you.

【18】* * *

【19】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. How to proceed with down syndrome result of 1:211 in my first month of pregnancy?
====================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Krutika Shrikant Ingle**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Nov 29, 2022 and last reviewed on: Nov 30, 2022_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】In my first month of pregnancy, I had a thyroid that increased to 19.1, but I got in control in 10 to 15 days. My dual marker test came positive for a down syndrome which is 1:211. I am worried.

【9】Please explain.

【10】Answered by Dr. Krutika Shrikant Ingle

【11】#

【12】Hi,

【13】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【14】As I can see on your report _(attachment removed to protect the patient's identity)_ , your gynecologist has also explained that further confirmatory tests would be required for diagnosing Down syndrome .

【15】This test is not accurate, but it definitely flags pregnancies. Hence, an amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling might be needed if the marker test comes positive. (The marker test is a screening test and has its limitations). But this would allow you to discuss with your husband and family how you want to proceed with the pregnancy . Would you want to take the chance, or would you like to terminate it?

【16】After discussing with your family, share and discuss your doubts and concerns with your gynecologist, then proceed further.

【17】I have some limitations in explaining everything here, and I have tried my best to explain it to you.

【18】I hope you understand.

【19】Regards.

【20】* * *

source_info.title: Does my double marker test result show chances of complications?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Does my double marker test result show chances of complications?
===================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Sameer Kumar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 10, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 17, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I want to know about the double marker test results. I am uploading the reports.

【9】Answered by Dr. Sameer Kumar

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I have seen the reports (attachment removed to protect patient identity) and understand your concern. The result is in the high-risk zone, and the next test would be a quadruple test done after two weeks to check for risk of aneuploidies.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor,

【16】Can you tell me what is to be done now? What are the chances of a complication? Should we be worried?

【17】Answered by Dr. Sameer Kumar

【18】#

【19】Hello,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】The next step would be to get a quadruple screening done at 13 to 15 weeks of gestation. If the risk of trisomy 21, 13 and 18 remain high, you will have to undergo amniocentesis or NIPT (non-invasive prenatal testing) to get fetal cell karyotyping done, to check for chromosomal aneuploidy. Also, there are 20 to 30 percent chances that these marker tests even if positive, deliver a normal child. Hence, karyotyping of foetus is a must.

【22】* * *

source_info.title: What causes the urge to urinate every 30 minutes?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What causes the urge to urinate every 30 minutes?
====================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Gajanan Shirpad Bhat**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr.Nithila A

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 21, 2019 and last reviewed on: Jul 14, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am 28 years old, 6feet, 190 lbs. For a couple of months, I have been experiencing the urge to urinate every 30 minutes or so. There is no burning, no aches, no pains, or nothing out of the ordinary. I can hold my bladder. There is no leaking. Even when I wake up in the morning, I am still keeping my bladder fine. I went to a family clinic and took blood work along with a urine sample. The doctor told me there is microscopic blood in my urine, but nothing else. The blood test came back negative for diabetes and any other abnormalities. However, she did say my kidneys seemed stressed. From what she saw on the blood work. As a young black male, I do suffer from high blood pressure. I fast, do a lot of cardio, and weight train. Even if I do not drink much water, I still urinate. When I do go, sometimes there is a lot that comes out, and some less. I do not smoke, and I do not drink. I am physically active. What can be causing this?

【9】Answered by Dr. Gajanan Shirpad Bhat

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Your symptoms are suggestive of an increased frequency of micturition . However, we need at least a single imaging study before we start treatment. The ideal one would be an ultrasound of the abdomen, pelvis with post-void residue. Please give more details about night time-frequency, flank pain as well as any history of previous catheterization. Also, I need to know the volume of each void and the total volume of intake and output per day. Do you have any difficulty in passing stools? If you can provide all these details, we can make a diagnosis and treat accordingly.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor,

【16】Now that scares me. I am not able to see a specialist until I see a doctor here (a few weeks from now). As far as night time-frequency, it is pretty much the same as during the day. I try to take sleeping pills so I can avoid the urination feeling so I could fall asleep. My volume is two to three cups when I do go. I try not to drink any fluids that much because I try not to go as much. Even if I do not drink much, I still go every 30 minutes. The urine is sometimes lemonade yellow or darker (not dehydrated dark though). I remember having very very very slight flank discomfort two months, but that went away fast. No difficulty passing stools and no previous catheterizations.

【17】Answered by Dr. Gajanan Shirpad Bhat

【18】#

【19】Hello,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】You need not be scared, as it appears just increased frequency, which does not suggest any significant disease or disorder. Thanks for the additional info provided by you, confirms a benign condition. However, I need at least an ultrasound abdomen pelvis with the post-void residue to start you on treatment. I hope you will get back to me with USG. I again reiterate you need not be scared, it is a benign treatable condition.

【22】* * *

source_info.title: Which other contraceptive pills can be used to prevent pregnancy after frequent sexual activity?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Which other contraceptive pills can be used to prevent pregnancy after frequent sexual activity?
===================================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Balakrishnan R**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 17, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I had unprotected sex today with my girlfriend, but she took the emergency contraceptive pill approximately five hours later. However, she has not experienced her period yet, and she is considering taking other tablets to induce it since her periods are irregular. Additionally, she has noticed a continuous flow of white-colored gel-like substances from her vagina after taking the I-pill. I am concerned if this is a good sign regarding pregnancy. Could you please advise if she might be pregnant?

【9】Furthermore, what steps should she take to terminate the pregnancy if she is pregnant? Should she take period-inducing tablets? I am extremely worried so I would appreciate your prompt assistance.

【10】Thank you.

【11】Answered by Dr. Balakrishnan R

【12】#

【13】Hello,

【14】Welcome to the icliniq family.

【15】I hope you are doing well.

【16】Explaining the complex hormonal balance that regulates periods and ovulation can be challenging. In the case of irregular periods, it becomes difficult to predict the ovulation date. The contraceptive pill contains a high dose of the hormone progesterone, which is naturally produced in the second half of the menstrual cycle after ovulation. This pill increases the thickness of the inner lining of the uterus, making it unfavorable for a potential pregnancy to implant. Since it is a single dose, it does not have enough strength to sustain itself, so the increased lining sheds off, resulting in bleeding or a period of seven to ten days. She does not need to take any other medication to induce periods. The white discharge she is experiencing could be normal vaginal discharge, remnants of semen flowing out, or a result of no ovulation. It is best not to worry about it. The best course of action is to wait for seven to ten days. She should get her period within this time frame. There are no other medications available to prevent pregnancy at this stage. To avoid pregnancy in the future, it is essential to consider better contraceptive methods. If you engage in frequent sexual activity, using cyclical oral contraceptive pills can be a highly effective method that helps regulate periods. If sexual activity is infrequent, using condoms is recommended.

【17】I hope I have addressed your concerns.

【18】Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions.

【19】Best regards.

【20】* * *

==========================================================================================

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jun 05, 2023 and last reviewed on: Jul 05, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am having sharp pain in my lower left abdomen during intercourse, in a position when I am on my hand and knees. This pain is a recent development and has not been a problem before. Also, I am not pregnant. And I am certain that I do not have an STI because my husband and I have never had sexual relations with anyone apart from ourselves. What could be the reason for this pain?

【9】Please help.

【10】Answered by Dr. Uzma Arqam

【11】#

【12】Hello,

【13】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【14】I have read your query and can understand your concern.

2.  Besides ectopic pregnancy, this type of pain can be due to endometrioma, local inflammatory lesions, or inflammatory cysts. The gold standard for diagnosis of endometrioma is a laparoscopy. If these investigations detect an endometrioma, then I suggest you take cyclic oral contraceptive pills for three to six months as it will reduce endometriosis pain and also provide contraception. I suggest you consult a specialist, talk with them, and take the medications with their consent.
3.  For pain relief associated with intercourse, I suggest you take a tablet of Ponstan (Mefenamic Acid) 500 mg around half an hour before intercourse.

【17】I hope this has helped you. Kindly follow up if you have more doubts.

【18】Thank you.

【19】* * *

source_info.title: Does using laptops for a longer duration make the eyes small?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Does using laptops for a longer duration make the eyes small?
================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Rahul Vaswani**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 13, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】My eyes have become smaller over the years. It did not happen all of a sudden. They have become smaller for a few years. I use the laptop for more than 10 hours a day. Does the problem occur due to increased use of a computer? Do I need to wear anti-glare or blue cut lenses? I am taking tablets for the thyroid problem for the past four years.

【9】Answered by Dr. Rahul Vaswani

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】You can share a close picture of your eyes. You might have drooping of eyelids which is known as ptosis. It gives an appearance of eyes getting smaller. When you are using a computer regularly, kindly follow these instructions. Display of your screen should have a good resolution. The height of the screen should be below the eye level. Move your eyes from the screen for every 20 minutes and gaze at an object as far as possible for 20 seconds and then get back to work. Blink your eyes for at least 15 to 20 times per minute. Whenever you click the mouse, try to blink. Take a break for every 45 minutes. Instill refresh tears eye drop to the eyes for four to six times a day. When your eyes feel tired, light your room. The light should come from behind your head, and it should not be in front of you.

【14】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Is plough pose and bending body inward in yoga bad for heart?
================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Isaac Gana**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. K Shobana

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Dec 28, 2021 and last reviewed on: Jul 13, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I have a question regarding my bicuspid aortic valve. I have mild aortic insufficiency, and my left ventricle was dilated. I am taking tablet Losartan 50 mg daily and practicing yoga (plough pose and the front bend). Does bending the body inward increase pressure on my heart? And does this pressure increase left ventricle dilatation and makes the aortic insufficiency worse? Kindly help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Isaac Gana

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Sorry to hear about your health issues. Bending inwards does not affect your health condition. I only advise that you do exercises moderately and stop if you have any shortness of breath or dizziness during any workout. Best regards.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Hi doctor,

【16】Thank you for the reply. I have attached two pictures. I can do the halasana pose with my legs over my head, but I wrap my arms around my buttocks and pull it down even further; I hurt my back and ribs. Would this cause heart pressure that makes my heart condition worse? Kindly help.

【17】Answered by Dr. Isaac Gana

【18】#

【19】Hi,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】I checked your pictures ( _attachments removed to protect the patient’s identity_ ). The exercises would not cause any pressure on your heart or affect circulation. For a healthier heart, I advise you to get involved in cardio exercises. Best regards.

【22】* * *

source_info.title: Can the axial length of the eye be decreased by 0.2 mm?
source_info.text:
【0】Can the axial length of the eye be decreased by 0.2 mm?
Listen

【1】Q. Can the axial length of the eye be decreased by 0. 2 mm?
===========================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Bandivadekar Pooja Mohan**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Sep 08, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 05, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】For a military medical test, I want to decrease the axial length of my eye by 0.2 mm. Can the axial length of the eye be decreased by 0.2 mm temporarily just for an eye checkup? I had myopia, but I got a LASIK done, so now I have a perfect vision.

【9】Answered by Dr. Bandivadekar Pooja Mohan

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Eye length cannot be decreased. However, if you are contemplating temporarily correcting your refractive error, then Ortho-K (orthokeratology) lenses are worth a try. They are worn overnight, and refractive error is corrected. But you have to use them every night. 0.2 mm change is usually within the preview of instrument error. A scan may note 23 mm as axial length and also as 23.2 mm in the next sitting.

【14】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I have very high cholesterol and blood sugar levels despite taking medications. Need help.
=============================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Prabhakaran**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Preetha J

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Oct 30, 2020 and last reviewed on: Jul 20, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I am a 62-year-old male who is 5 feet tall and weighs about 175 pounds. I am a vegetarian, I have diabetes for the past 20 years, and my blood pressure is normal. Sometimes my cholesterol is high, and after taking Stanlip 145 mg tablet (one per day), it used to come down, but for the past month, I am not taking it, and in my recent blood test report, it has gone high. Earlier, for many years, I had a Gluconorm-G2 tablet (twice per day), Januvia 100 mg tablet twice daily, and Volix 0.2 mg tablet once daily. I met a doctor last year, and he asked me to change my food habit to low carbohydrates and moderate protein, and high fat; after following his diet schedule, I have reduced 9 pounds and stopped taking Gluconorm-G2 and Volix tablets, and was active till seven months back. After COVID-19, I could not follow the diet, and now when I checked the blood test this month, and found that my blood sugar level and cholesterol level are increased. I also take Clopitab 75 mg and Zincovit tablet 1 per day. I have attached my various blood test reports. Based on these reports, can you please suggest medications?

【9】Answered by Dr. Prabhakaran

【10】#

【11】Hello,

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I noticed an itchy, raised and hard lesion on my scalp. What is that?
========================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Shalini Patodiya**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jan 14, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 06, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I noticed a scalp lesion two months ago. It is a bit scaly if scratched, hard and raised. I would like to peel it off, but it is not getting removed. But, I did not notice any hair loss. Other than a little bit of itching of the scalp, there is no issue.

【9】Answered by Dr. Shalini Patodiya

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】It can be scalp psoriasis or warts. Please send me a photo to diagnose the condition and suggest you treatment.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Hi doctor,

【16】Please see the photos attached. Thank you.

【17】Answered by Dr. Shalini Patodiya

【18】#

【19】Hi,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】This does not look like psoriasis or wart. It looks like prurigo ( _attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ). Prurigo is an itchy nodule. The more you itch, the more it worsens. I suggest you the following treatment. Consult your specialist doctor, discuss with him or her and take treatment with consent.

【22】1.  Apply Topisal-S 6% lotion (Clobetasol and Salicylic acid) every night.
2.  Tablet Levosiz (Levocetirizine) once daily.

【23】This should resolve the lesion within two weeks. Please try not to scratch.

【24】Patient's Query

【25】Thank you doctor,

【26】Are you sure that it is not a ringworm or any other fungal infection?

【27】Answered by Dr. Shalini Patodiya

【28】#

【29】Hello,

【30】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【31】Fungal infections of the scalp are uncommon at this age and also they look different. I am sure that it is not ringworm or fungal infection.

【32】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I am suffering from warts and molluscum. How did I get the infection?
========================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Shalini Patodiya**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jan 30, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 07, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am a 24-year-old male. Last year, I had a few molluscum contagiosum in my lower abdomen. I took the treatment, and they were gone. After two to three months, I got one skin tag on the skin around my penis. I applied a lotion (Salicylic acid 16.7% and Lactic acid 16.7%), and the skin tag was removed. But, it came back after three months. Currently, I am suffering from genital warts and taking treatment.

【9】My doctor told me to get some tests and here are the results. Lipid profile - triglycerides 125 mg/dL, HDL 35 mg/dL and LDL 113 mg/dL, CBC - lymphocyte 44%, serum amylase 121 IU/L, Helicobacter pylori IgA 0.45 (negative) and urine test - pus cells 3 to 4/HPF. Currently, I am taking these medicine as advised by my doctor. Zincolak one tablet twice daily, Zycolchin one tablet twice daily, and Dicaris 150 mg one tablet once a day for three days.

【10】My question is that I am a healthy man with high immunity. I never get sick all around the year. How did I catch this infection? I have multiple sex partners, but I never had sex without a condom, or my condom never broke. Please give me a detailed answer and also give me advice for the treatment.

【11】Answered by Dr. Shalini Patodiya

【12】#

【13】Hello,

【14】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【15】Warts and molluscum are common sexually acquired infections and can occur in healthy individuals. Warts spread by touch and condoms will only protect the covered area. Base of the penis, thighs, lower abdomen are all exposed. So, both warts and molluscum can be transmitted even with condom usage. For treatment, I suggest you Imiquimod 5% cream. Apply it over the affected area thrice a week and leave it overnight and wash in the morning. Use it for 16 weeks. Consult your specialist doctor, discuss with him or her and take treatment with consent. Also, you should get tested for HIV and hepatitis.

【16】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Why am I having patches on chest and back?
=============================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Touseef Ansar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 29, 2018 and last reviewed on: Sep 16, 2020_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am just now noticing these patches on my skin and would like your input. My skin does not itch but I have been noticing patches on my chest and it is all over my back.

【9】Answered by Dr. Touseef Ansar

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】These patches are due to fungal activity. Let me suggest you some medicines. You should apply and give me feedback.

【14】* * *

【15】**The Probable causes:**  

【16】Moist wet skin.

【17】**Investigations to be done:**  

【18】KOH (potassium hydroxide) scrapping and microscopy.

【19】**Probable diagnosis:**  

【20】**Tinea versicolor** .

【21】**Treatment plan:**  

【22】1\. Wash with Ketoconazole lotion once daily.  
2\. Apply Terbinafine cream twice daily.  
3\. Take capsule Fluconazole 150 mg once only.

【23】**Regarding follow up:**  

【24】For more information consult a **dermatologist online** .---> https://www.icliniq.com/ask-a-doctor-online/dermatologist

【25】* * *
