source_info.title: Is this growing spot on my face a young melanoma?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Is this growing spot on my face a young melanoma?
====================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Ashwini. V. Swamy**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Feb 14, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 20, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I recently had a melanoma in situ removed from my left middle finger knuckle. This has caused us to look more closely at other areas of the body. There is a small spot that was not there four months ago under my left eye. I started seeing it in photos after that faintly. It is now more defined and a lot easier to see in photos. It is still only about 2 to 3 mm and pretty faint. The dermatologist looked at it and said it was a bit raised compared to the other spots that looked like sun spots. She then froze all three. I am concerned this growing spot is a very young melanoma (since it is growing). It is been three days and the scab already peeled off and it seems to still be there (although that could be irritation from the freezing). How long do I need to go back and have it biopsied to know? I can send photos if needed.

【9】Answered by Dr. Ashwini. V. Swamy

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I saw your clinical pictures ( _attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ). In your recent picture, the lesion looks like seborrheic keratosis (harmless), it looks rough and raised. I cannot confirm what it is with this picture. I am sorry dear, the picture becomes little blurry when I try to zoom it, to appreciate finer features. I am very sure your dermatologist would have looked at the spot with adermoscope. With dermoscopy, the dermatologist can make out abnormal changes that are concerning. Even if it is doubtful feature leaning towards melanoma, your dermatologist would have done a shave biopsy to rule out that minimal possibility. After cryotherapy, the area becomes dark, it scabs and falls off after five to seven days.

【14】I can understand your concern as you had a melanoma in situ removed recently. Observe the treated spot for another week, allow the spot to heal completely. After a week, if you feel it is still there, then you can undergo shave biopsy which would say precisely what it is.

【15】Regards.

【16】Patient's Query

【17】Hello doctor,

【18】Thank you for your quick and thoughtful reply.

【19】Since the melanoma diagnosis, I have had a hard time looking at any spot that grows like this. She did look at it with the special derm tool to look closer. Can I ask a few questions?

【20】1.  Can a seborrheic keratosis appear so quickly? (Few months)
2.  I have other similar-looking spots on my face, but they are not rough or raised. Is it normal for a spot like this to be different like that than the others?
3.  If it is melanoma in its early stages, will it still appear that way on a biopsy even if it was previously frozen?

【21】I had shown my melanoma spot to two dermatologists and when I still did not feel good about it, I saw a third and he took it. It was small, had clear borders, symmetric, and was only one color. The only strange thing was that it just looked very different than any other freckle and was growing and getting darker over time (I attached a photo). It is hard now as I am very afraid of every other spot on my body and do not want anyone to overlook a bad spot like the last time. I am just really scared.

【22】Answered by Dr. Ashwini. V. Swamy

【23】#

【24】Hello,

【25】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【26】Let me address all your concerns, one by one. Can a seborrheic keratosis appear so quickly? (Few months) - Yes, it can appear over few weeks to months. These are also called age spots usually seen in adults and elderly, very harmless. I mentioned seborrheic keratosis because it was appearing raised, and little rough in that picture.

【27】I have other similar looking spots on my face, but they are not rough or raised. Is it normal for a spot like this to be different like that than the others? Lentigines or sun spots, freckles are very common in fair type 2 skin people. If the spot is constantly under friction like rubbing, wearing eyeglasses, with pressure on those spots, it can become slightly thick and appear raised.

【28】If it is a melanoma in early stages, will it still appear that way on a biopsy even if it was previously frozen? A pathologist will be able to see cancerous features even after cryotherapy if the spot is still there. After the biopsy, if there are no cancer cells that means it was not a melanoma or it is totally gone. There are staining methods where they can find even the slightest cancerous change in the tissue. A pathologist will be very cautious while seeing the biopsy if the history of previous melanoma has been provided to him.

【29】Melanoma in situ is the early stage cancer, they have caught it and removed it with wide surgical excision. It is good to be cautious about any similar spots, new moles, changes in the existing mole, like:

【30】A- Asymmetry, B- Border changes/Bleeding, C- Color change (darkening), D- Diameter changes (enlarging).

【31】I can make a clinical diagnosis with what appears on this picture, but any cancerous feature needs to confirmed by biopsy. Allow a week to pass, so that it heals. See if the spot is still there. If yes, then you can go for shave biopsy (minimal pigmentation/scar from shave biopsy).

【32】Hope I have answered your concerns to the best of my knowledge.

【33】* * *

===============================================

【8】I have pronounced laugh lines since I was 15, and now I am trying to get rid of them. I tried coconut oil but it is not working. I also have lines around my eyes and I do not know what to do. Please help me.

【11】Hello,

【14】Patient's Query

【19】Hello,

【21】Most patients get this done when they are over 40, but there is no age limit. Any person can get Botox or filler at any age. source_info.title: Can I get Naegleria fowleri infection from washing my nose with tap water?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can I get Naegleria fowleri infection from washing my nose with tap water?
=============================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Kumar Ashutosh**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Oct 21, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 11, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am in a subtropical state. As I was washing my face a few days ago, I accidentally got some tap water up my nose. Vaguely aware that there might be concerns about the Naegleria fowleri amoeba down here, I panicked and then took some bottled mineral water and tried to rinse my nose with it, thinking that that might be more thoroughly purified and wash away anything from the tap water. However, the bottled water ended up going much further up my nose, and it felt the way it used to feel when getting water up my nose in a swimming pool as a kid. That happened a few days ago. I am worried whether either of these water sources (tap and/or bottled water) could have contained the amoeba. I have been having some issues with mucus dripping from the back of my nose into my throat, occasionally mild pressure when I swallow, and for the past couple of days I have had a vague headache all day, but nothing intensely painful (it seems to have diminished somewhat today, though perhaps not fully gone away). I am not sure if I should go to an ER for evaluation, or if I should just wait and see if any more characteristic symptoms develop. I have not observed any changes in smelling ability, nor any neck pain; just a mild, vague headache. I know that if one gets the Naegleria fowleri infection time is of the essence, but I do not want to go spend a lot of money and time at the ER just to have them say that they do not see anything yet and to come back if anything changes. Is there a test they could do at this point to determine if an amoeba is present, or is that only practicable if an infection reaches a more serious stage? Should I go to an emergency room now or just wait and see what happens?

【9】Answered by Dr. Kumar Ashutosh

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Firstly, do not worry at all. Please let me know exactly how many days have passed after the exposure. Also, know these facts: Naegleria infection is very rare. Less than 200 cases are reported till date. It spreads very rapidly and symptoms appear within five to 10 days of exposure. Symptoms include a sudden onset of a severe headache, rhinitis, nausea, vomiting and neck stiffness, which later progress to rapid deterioration. The lab test that is available is CSF (cerebrospinal fluid) examination under a microscope. My advice is to take tablet Montair-LC (a combination of Montelukast and Levocetirizine) at bedtime for five days and steam inhalation for rhinitis. Consult your specialist doctor, discuss with him or her and start taking the medicines with their consent. If you develop any of the above symptoms, do consult a doctor immediately, but if it is already more than 10 days of exposure, there is a very minimal chance of this infection. Revert to me when you feel like. Thanks. Have a great day.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Hello doctor,

【16】Thank you for your time. Both the recent exposures occurred approximately three and a half days ago. The bottled water went much further up my nose than the tap water, and although it is supposedly purified, it is not sterile. I think this bottled water originates from surface water in several southern states, and the company is very unwilling to provide additional details about its purification beyond what is on their website. After the bottled water exposure, I very briefly tried steaming over some boiled water with a towel. I only did this for several seconds, however, I thought that the steam going up my nose was too hot. If I had burned the interior of my nasal cavity with the steam, could it cause a headache-like feeling behind my eyes and in the front of my head? Also, do you recommend not going to an ER unless things get notably worse? Would they only do the test you mentioned if the more serious kinds of symptoms developed? I only ask this because I thought that that kind of test took a couple of weeks to process or complete, so that the longer one waited, the less useful the results might be with something that can move so quickly if it strikes.

【17】Answered by Dr. Kumar Ashutosh

【18】#

【19】Hello,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】Naegleria infection is very rare. Already four days have passed since the last exposure. So, do not worry much.Take anti-allergics as I mentioned.Do visit the ER, if you develop high-grade fever, vomiting, headache, or neck stiffness. But, the chances are very less. Revert to me after 10 to 15 days.

【22】* * *

source_info.title: I have a mark on my toe. Can this be melanoma?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I have a mark on my toe. Can this be melanoma?
=================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Sushil Kakkar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jun 16, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 25, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I have a mark on my toe that has been there a few years and although my GP was not concerned, I am very scared it could be melanoma. It has not changed dramatically but it could have changed subtly as in some photos it looks a little darker and others a little bigger, although it is hard to tell due to changes in lighting.

【9】Answered by Dr. Sushil Kakkar

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I have viewed the images ( _attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ). It seems a benign nevus, well-defined, regular, and uniformly colored. Moreover, it has not changed over the years. However, dermoscopy is the best way to be sure about that, as benign nevi have pigment along the furrows rather than the ridges of plantar dermatoglyphics (parallel furrow pattern) whereas melanoma also has pigment along the ridges (parallel ridge pattern) on dermoscopy.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor,

【16】I have looked at the photos of the parallel and ridge patterns online and from looking at that photo of my toe it seems like **there is a lot of pigment on the ridges, not just the furrows** . Also, there are some dots around the edges if you zoom in and also some that are hard to see unless you look in person, on the ridges themselves that I have read could be infiltrated eccrine ducts which are even worse. **Are you able to tell these things just by looking or am I jumping to conclusions** ? From the photos of furrow patterns I looked at it looked like pigment was in the furrows only.

【17】Answered by Dr. Sushil Kakkar

【18】#

【19】Hi,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】Naked eye is not good enough to correctly delineate the pattern. I suggest dermoscopy. Moreover, **a lattice pattern, which is a subtype of parallel furrow pattern can look like your nevus with a naked eye** . The white dots on ridges are openings of eccrine ducts or sweat gland and is perfectly normal.

【22】For more information consult a **dermatologist online** \--> https://www.icliniq.com/ask-a-doctor-online/dermatologist

【23】Patient's Query

【24】Hi doctor,

【25】Thanks for your reply. The dots I was referring to are not white. **There are some white dots but also some of them are brown** . Does that mean it is automatically parallel ridge?

【26】Answered by Dr. Sushil Kakkar

【27】#

【28】Hi,

【29】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【30】**I think those brown specks or dots are just part of the lattice pattern rather than infiltrated ducts** . They do not seem to be of concern. Still, I would suggest dermoscopy.

【31】For more information consult a **dermatologist online** \--> https://www.icliniq.com/ask-a-doctor-online/dermatologist

【32】* * *

source_info.title: Can topical steroid cream help in healing the red spots on my nose?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can topical steroid cream help in healing the red spots on my nose?
======================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Sushil Kakkar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Aug 10, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I got red patches on my nose after using chemically made facial products while using Retin-A ointment. I have attached pictures. In that, I have used Cerave ointment for healing the marks. Now, I discontinued using Retin-A 0.025 % ointment.

【9】Answered by Dr. Sushil Kakkar

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I have gone through the attachment ( _attachment removed to protect patient identity_ ). Retin-A (Tretinoin) makes the skin sensitive and a scrub or facial may cause dermatitis like this. I suggest you use a moderately potent topical steroid cream like Fluticasone propionate 0.05 % cream or Mometasone furoate 0.1 % cream, twice daily for a week. It will get fine.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor,

【16】Red spots will not heal without a steroid cream. I am a little scared of putting anything on my face. But can I use sunscreen or moisturizer on my face? Is it fine? Are you sure these steroid creams will heal it?

【17】Answered by Dr. Sushil Kakkar

【18】#

【19】Hi,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】Yes, you can use a moisturizer for a few days that would be fine. However, a topical steroid cream would heal it faster. Without steroid cream, it would take a longer time to recover.

【22】* * *

source_info.title: I get itchy dry eyes after prolonged screentime with occasional vision loss. Why?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I get itchy dry eyes after prolonged screentime with occasional vision loss. Why?
====================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Shikha Gupta**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Vinodhini. J

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 30, 2020 and last reviewed on: Jul 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My eyes hurt for about a week now. I feel like resting for a long period of time. They are itchy and dry. There is a foreign object sensation. Sometimes, I feel like I am losing my vision or it is getting weaker. Sometimes I do the 20-20-20 rule. Lately, I have been spending a lot of time in front of the screen. What could be the reason my eyes hurt? Currently, I am taking Isotretinoin 20 mg twice a day, and Topical Benzoyl Peroxide 5% and topical Retinoid and Clindamycin for chronic acne.

【9】Answered by Dr. Shikha Gupta

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】You must get your BP, and blood sugar levels done. Monitor if normal or abnormal and consult a physician. Also, get 2D echo done as soon as possible and seek a cardiologist opinion. The condition that you lost vision suddenly for some time is known as amaurosis fugax. I am telling you this first because this is serious. Also, it is a must to get your refraction done and also consult a retina specialist and get the detailed retinal examination done as well. Coming to your eye symptoms, it would have been better if you share a picture of eyes but it seems like you have allergic symptoms. I hope there is no discharge or stickiness of eyes. You can use Bepotastine 1.5% eye drop TDS one drop in both eyes for two weeks. Soft drops 0.5% (Sodium carboxymethylcellulose) eye drop six times a day (one drop in both eyes) for one month. Avoid any rubbing of eyes. Use goggles.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: What are the tests to be done before marrying a close relative?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What are the tests to be done before marrying a close relative?
==================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Singh Smrita**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Aug 14, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 24, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】As suggested by most of the doctor marrying a girl with the same blood group will not cause any problems, in my case the blood group is A+ve. She is my maternal uncle's daughter. She is a close relative. Can our marriage create a reduced genetic pool? Can I marry the girl? Will I have kids if I marry her? Will I have a future kid without genetic defects? What are tests needed to be done if I want to marry the girl in close relation first or second order? As I have read reduced genetic pool can create abnormalities as common genes which are suppressed may become active in the next generation. Please guide in this issue.

【9】Answered by Dr. Singh Smrita

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】As you want to marry within your related family, I would suggest that you get yourself and your fiance genetically tested to estimate the risks based on both your genetic profiles. This will greatly help you with determining the chances of the child having genetic defects.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor,

【16】Which genetic test needs to be done?

【17】Answered by Dr. Singh Smrita

【18】#

【19】Hello,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】**These recommendations are the opinions of a multicenter working group (the Consanguinity Working Group (CWG))** with expertise in genetic counseling, medical genetics, biochemical genetics, genetic epidemiology, pediatrics, perinatology, and public health genetics, which was convened by the National Society of Genetic Counselors (NSGC). The consensus of the CWG and NSGC reviewers is that beyond a thorough medical family history with follow-up of significant findings, no additional preconception screening is recommended for consanguineous couples.

【22】**During pregnancy, consanguineous couples should be offered maternal-fetal serum marker screening and high-resolution fetal ultrasonography** . Newborns should be screened for impaired hearing and detection of treatable inborn errors of metabolism. Since, you said that there is a history of a child being born in your family with developmental anomalies, the cause of the malformation should be determined. A thorough family history will be taken by your doctor for at least 3 to 4 generations. Based on the history, further tests will be recommended.

【23】For more information consult a **hematologist online** \--> https://www.icliniq.com/ask-a-doctor-online/hematologist

【24】* * *

source_info.title: I am having symptomless large tonsil, it does not bother unless I look at it. Kindly guide.
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I am having symptomless large tonsil, it does not bother unless I look at it. Kindly guide.
==============================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Shyam Kalyan. N**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr.Nithila A

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 23, 2019 and last reviewed on: Jul 27, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I have one larger tonsil and there are no symptoms. It does not bother me unless I look at it.

【9】Answered by Dr. Shyam Kalyan. N

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】One-sided enlarged tonsil is not a good thing to have. Usually, when both sides are enlarged, it would mean an infection or chronic infections over tonsils and pharynx. Unilateral enlargement needs to be investigated to rule out a tumor or abnormal growth. If you were to show to me, I would go for a tonsillectomy surgery where I remove both side tonsils and send them separately for biopsy (histopathological examination). That will give us a final report on what exactly it is.

【14】Patient's Query

【15】Thank you doctor,

【16】What are the chances of tumor? I have this as long as I can remember.

【17】Answered by Dr. Shyam Kalyan. N

【18】#

【19】Hello,

【20】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【21】Considering the long-standing history of the enlargement without any symptom and your age and assuming you do not use tobacco in any form, the chances of malignancy or cancer is less. But there are some chances of it being a benign tumor. But this being a unilateral enlargement it is best removed and biopsied.

【22】* * *

source_info.title: Would viral infection affect the lymphocyte and neutrophil values?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Would viral infection affect the lymphocyte and neutrophil values?
=====================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Goswami Parth Rajendragiri**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Aug 17, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I had a viral infection last week. Is it normal to have increased lymphocyte levels of 52 % and decreased neutrophil levels of 35 % after having a viral infection? It got healed within a week. I was fine when I did my blood test. My RBC and WBC are considered to be normal. As I have anemia, my platelet levels are high. I am worried. Also how long should I need to wait for rechecking my blood test? When would these levels of lymphocytes and neutrophils be recovered? Would urinary infections also affect them?

【9】Answered by Dr. Goswami Parth Rajendragiri

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】After having a viral infection , lymphocytosis can persist for seven to ten days. Your low neutrophils are relative, and it is because of increased lymphocytes. Platelet can be high because of inflammation or by iron deficiency anemia as a reactive thrombocytosis . Urinary infection can also lead to such a presentation. You can repeat CBC (complete blood count) after a week. Attach your reports to guide you further.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: Why do I have severe menstrual cramps and abdominal pain for many years?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Why do I have severe menstrual cramps and abdominal pain for many years?
===========================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Balakrishnan R**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 11, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I am a 28-year-old with a height of 5 feet 2 inches and a weight of 50 kg. I am newly married. Since I was 14 years old, I have been bearing menstrual cramps, which result in very severe lower abdominal pain. Please help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Balakrishnan R

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I understand your concern.

【14】Let me start by saying that this is quite normal for this age. During the initial few years, the periods are irregular or even regular, and the uterus is still immature for seven days, just developing into healthy adult-size. So every month, when you get periods, you may have a few blood clots and thick fleshy masses sometimes. This is more than normal bleeding. This has to pass through the narrow cervical canal. This is very painful, as the cervical canal or mouth of the uterus (the lower end which opens into the vagina) is very firm and will not yield. So this causes excruciating pain till the main bulk of blood or clots is gone. You will be immediately relieved of pain after that clot goes, to get it again in the next periods when the heavy bleeding is about to start (usually within the first and second days only). You can have relief by taking precautionary painkillers like Meftal-Spas (Dicyclomine and Mefenamic acid) just before the pain. You will have a permanent solution only after the cervix is permanently dilated, which occurs after a normal vaginal delivery of the baby. Now since you are newly married, you may also have pain during the end of sex also, or also during passing urine. They will go away on their own. You do not need any medications.

【15】Hope I have clarified your query, do write back if any more queries.

【16】All the best.

【17】* * *

source_info.title: What is the chance of pregnancy in PCOS?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What is the chance of pregnancy in PCOS?
===========================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Dattaprasad Balasaheb Inamdar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Nov 05, 2016 and last reviewed on: Jul 04, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I have PCOS and have not had a period for over a year. Now, I have a partner and we do not use protection. Two days ago, I woke up with a light bleed and that lasted for a few hours and disappeared. Then, the same thing happened today and I bled for a few hours. I took a pregnancy test and it was negative. I have body pain and my breasts are tender.

【9】Answered by Dr. Dattaprasad Balasaheb Inamdar

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】With so much prolonged **amenorrhea ,** ovulation is unlikely to have occurred and pregnancy is less likely. Kindly use barrier contraceptive (condom) for three weeks and repeat home pregnancy test. If it comes negative, then pregnancy is almost ruled out. Absence of menstrual cycle for such a long term is not desirable, as it increases the chance of endometrial cancer by unopposed estrogen exposure to endometrium. It is a good practice to induce withdrawal bleeding by taking progesterone tablets for every two to three months. Kindly consult your doctor for the same and for other risk reduction strategies.

【14】* * *

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I am on Insulin for diabetes. Could I get treated with oral drugs?
=====================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Qazi Mujahid Ali**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr.Nithila A

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Sep 18, 2019 and last reviewed on: Jul 11, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I had been diagnosed as a person with diabetes before 10 years. Now I am taking Amaryl MV 2 bd dosage. Still, my rbs is around 250 to 270 mg/dL. What I need to do? Is there any possibility that I can avoid insulin therapy and by oral therapy only I can be treated? And now I think I am facing problems with neuropathy also. Pain in the palm and numbness in the feet even some sexual issues also. Please suggest to me what kind of treatment I should follow.

【9】Answered by Dr. Qazi Mujahid Ali

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】You are facing complications of diabetes, to control sugar you can take Glimipride 3 mg before breakfast and Sitagliptin Metformin 50/500 mg twice daily after breakfast and dinner. Avoid junk food, fatty meals, and deep-fried items along with sugary drinks. Brisk walk for 25 minutes for five days a week. Avoid anxieties try to relax. Eat Short meals instead of three meals, I mean divide your daily meal into small portions.

【14】* * *

【15】**The Probable causes:**  

【16】The probable cause is complications faced due to uncontrolled diabetes.

【17】**Investigations to be done:**  

【18】Do HbA1c (glycated hemoglobin), lipid profile, serum creatinine, urine analysis and fasting blood sugar.

【19】* * *

source_info.title: I have erectile dysfunction and ejaculation problems. Please advise.
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I have erectile dysfunction and ejaculation problems. Please advise.
=======================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Karthik Rajan**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 13, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My cum is not coming out by force or thrust. The cum is just flowing out of my penis. Three years earlier the cum was coming out by force or thrust. I am having erectile dysfunction may be since last two years or two and half years, and I was not having erectile disfunction earlier. I am taking Megalis 20 and Tentex Forte prescribed by a doctor and through these medicines, I am having a proper erection. I am having only one testicle, my another testicle was removed when I was of 13 years due to its under development. I want to have my cum come out by thrust or force from my penis to have a baby as I am married. I am 37 years of age, and my height is 5 feet 8 inches.

【9】Answered by Dr. Karthik Rajan

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I have gone through your query. I would like to know whether the amount of semen ejaculated had been the same over the last three years or has it decreased? Firstly, the speed with which the ejaculate came out does not unduly affect your fertility. I would suggest you have a semen examination if not done before to check for the sperm count which is more important. Secondly coming to your complaint, I would ideally like to do a full physical examination given your previous history. It could either be some blockage in the path of semen or the semen could be going back into the bladder. I would suggest you to visit your local urologist for a detailed clinical examination, an ultrasound to check if there is any blockage and a semen test to check for the volume and sperm count. You can upload your reports and get an online erectile dysfunction prescription if required. Another possibility is incoordination of the muscles that normally gives the speed to the ejaculate, which cannot be tested to identify. As I said before, if your primary concern is to have a child, then I would suggest you to get a semen analysis first. If it is normal then you do not have anything to worry about.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: Is it safe to get a mole removed?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Is it safe to get a mole removed?
====================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Suvash Sahu**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Sep 22, 2016 and last reviewed on: Jul 05, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I have a small, flat mole on my nose bridge. How can I remove it? Please recommend the best method with your professional advice.

【9】Answered by Dr. Suvash Sahu

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I have seen your query and concern.

【14】With your descriptions, since the mole is flat means you have a superficial melanocytic nevus. If you want to get it removed, then I would recommend you shave excision under local anesthesia by a dermatologist. This procedure has very good cosmetic results. I have done around thousand of cases with this procedure with minimal to no scarring. The other options are TCA (trichloroacetic acid) cautery, radiofrequency cautery and Nd:YAG laser treatment (Neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet).

【15】Patient's Query

【16】Thank you doctor,

【17】Is shave excision a painful procedure? Do you think laser as a better option? What are the side effects? I heard somewhere that it is not a good idea to get a mole removed as it can contain cancer cells. How true is this?

【18】Answered by Dr. Suvash Sahu

【19】#

【20】Hi,

【21】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【22】Shave excision done under local anesthesia is a single-sitting procedure. In this Xylocaine, 2% 1 mL (Lidocaine) will be given in an insulin syringe, which is a tiny one. So, little pin prick pain occurs and after that the area gets numb. You will not feel any pain. Laser treatment requires five to six sitting in the gap of one-month intervals and after that, the chances of recurrence are more with this. You have wrong perceptions regarding mole excision. If you do not remove this, then the chance of getting cancer is more. So, better you get it removed.

【23】* * *

【1】Q. Is it safe to get a mole removed?
====================================

【2】<mark>Answered by

【3】Dr. Suvash Sahu

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】This is a premium question & answer published on Sep 22, 2016 and last reviewed on: Jul 05, 2023

【6】Patient’s Query</mark>nt's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I have a small, flat mole on my nose bridge. How can I remove it? Please recommend the best method with your professional advice.

【9】<mark>Answered by Dr. Suvash Sahu

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.</mark>

【13】I have seen your query and concern.

【14】With your descriptions, since the mole is flat means you have a superficial melanocytic nevus. If you want to get it removed, then I would recommend you shave excision under local anesthesia by a dermatologist. This procedure has very good cosmetic results. I have done around thousand of cases with this procedure with minimal to no scarring. The other options are TCA (trichloroacetic acid) cautery, radiofrequency cautery and Nd:YAG laser treatment (Neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet).

【15】Patient's Query

【16】Thank you doctor,

【17】Is shave excision a painful procedure? Do you think laser as a better option? What are the side effects? I heard somewhere that it is not a good idea to get a mole removed as it can contain cancer cells. How true is this?

【18】Answered by Dr. Suvash Sahu

【19】#

【20】Hi,

【21】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【22】Shave excision done under local anesthesia is a single-sitting procedure. In this Xylocaine, 2% 1 mL (Lidocaine) will be given in an insulin syringe, which is a tiny one. So, little pin prick pain occurs and after that the area gets numb. You will not feel any pain. Laser treatment requires five to six sitting in the gap of one-month intervals and after that, the chances of recurrence are more with this. You have wrong perceptions regarding mole excision. If you do not remove this, then the chance of getting cancer is more. So, better you get it removed.

source_info.title: How long does it take for facial swelling that occurred after a PMMA filler take to subside?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. How long does it take for facial swelling that occurred after a PMMA filler take to subside?
===============================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Pavan N Murdeshwar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 16, 2023 and last reviewed on: Jul 12, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I got a PMMA filler, and my face is extremely swollen. My face looks absolutely huge, and I am desperate and scared that it will not go back to normal. I got it on my jaw, 4.5 mL on each side, but it is so swollen. I cannot sleep thinking that I might have ruined my face forever. My doctor first prescribed me a corticosteroid injection that I do not recall the name of. Then after showing him photographs of the swelling on the second day, he prescribed Prednisone , which I took about eight hours ago. Should it not have shown results by now? I cannot look like this. Please help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Pavan N Murdeshwar

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I thoroughly read your query and understand your concern.

【14】I saw the picture ( _attachments are hidden to protect the patient's identity_ ) you sent. Definitely, you are having a lot of swelling, and I can understand your concerns. The PMMA (polymethylmethacrylate) filler , 4.5 mL on each side, is not much of a problem. In a few cases, it might cause such a kind of swelling, and a steroid will help. Prednisone especially will start acting after a few hours. So my suggestion is to wait until it starts its action. However, it might take somewhere from two to three weeks for most of that swelling to come down. Do not worry for now.

【15】Hope this has answered your query.

【16】Kind regards.

【17】* * *

【1】Q. I have lumps on my anus and it is growing larger. Why?
=========================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Alexander Davis**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Lochana

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Nov 04, 2020 and last reviewed on: Jul 10, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I have a lump on my anus and recently, it has become larger. I am worried about it.

【9】Answered by Dr. Alexander Davis

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Having a lump on the anus suddenly indicates a benign condition. You need to consult a doctor for having an examination. It seems like an anal venous thrombosis. There is nothing to be worried. If this diagnosis is confirmed by consulting a doctor, then you need to wait until they vanish as they appeared suddenly. The main reason for having it is due to much pressure produced while using bathroom. Thank you.

【14】* * *

【15】**The Probable causes:**  

【16】The probable cause is anal venous thrombosis.

【17】**Investigations to be done:**  

【18】The investigation to be done is a visual inspection by consulting a local general practitioner.

【19】**Differential diagnosis:**  

【20】Differential diagnoses are cysts, prolapsed hemorrhoids, and warts.

【21】**Probable diagnosis:**  

【22】The probable diagnosis is cysts, prolapsed hemorrhoids, and warts.

【23】**Treatment plan:**  

【24】The treatment plan consists of having an appointment by consulting a general practitioner. If your diagnosis is confirmed, you need to wait some time to resolve it.

【25】**Preventive measures:**  

【26】Preventive measures are to have regulation of stools by taking low-dose magnesium supplements.

【27】**Regarding follow up:**  

【28】Follow-up at any time.

source_info.text:

【1】Q. My fasting sugar is 194 and postprandial is 354. Am I diabetic?
==================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Suneetha B S**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. K Shobana

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Aug 14, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 07, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】Fasting blood sugar is 194 mg/dL and postprandial blood sugar is 354 mg/dL. Please tell me if sugar is confirmed or not. If I am diabetic, what should I do?

【9】Answered by Dr. Suneetha B S

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Looking at your blood sugar level, it is on the higher side. You will need medication to bring it under control. After a few months of treatment, your doctor will decide whether the dose can be reduced depending on your blood sugar control. As of now, it is important for you to start therapy and bring this under control. Remember, diabetes is not a disease by itself if it is under control. If the levels remain high constantly, it could lead to disease. Hence, I recommend that you visit your doctor as soon as possible for further guidance.

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. My granny has eye pain and light sensitivity for the past one week. Please suggest solution.
===============================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Shikha Gupta**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Vinodhini. J

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 11, 2020 and last reviewed on: Jul 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My grandmother is 83 years old and has been suffering from a mild form of glaucoma for three years now. When we consulted doctors earlier they suggested using eye drops than surgery. So we have been using Travo Z and Tear Drops daily and she is also able to see properly. Since one week she is experiencing pain in her eyes and has trouble looking at the light directly. Her eyes have also turned reddish. Please help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Shikha Gupta

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Has she got operated for cataract? Any previous record of vision please share the latest one. Also, share the glaucoma test reports in which she was diagnosed as glaucoma and share the photo of eyes.

【14】Patient's Query

source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can diabetes or jaundice cause growing painful lumps on the tongue?
======================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Suneetha B S**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Dec 06, 2022 and last reviewed on: Jul 21, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My dad had jaundice last month and got cured after medication. This week, he took a blood test, and all was normal except for his sugar level. He already has sugar problems and is taking medication. He has got small lumps on his tongue that are painful and growing big. He also got a fever yesterday and today. Is he having any problem with jaundice, or are lumps formed because of sugar?

【9】Answered by Dr. Suneetha B S

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I read your query and can understand your concern. I am not sure what you mean by lumps on the tongue. Are you talking about painful mouth ulcers or small painful eruptions on the tongue? If yes, it could be due to dehydration or vitamin B deficiency. In that case, I recommend that he should drink lots of water to keep himself hydrated. He can also take B-complex vitamins once a day for two weeks. He should also avoid spicy food and tea/coffee till he feels better. If you think these are not mouth ulcers , please send some pictures of his lesions on the tongue. It will help us arrive at a better diagnosis. I hope that helps. Thank you and take care.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: How to manage moderate hydronephrosis, hydroureter, and renal calculi?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. How to manage moderate hydronephrosis, hydroureter, and renal calculi?
=========================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Yash Kathuria**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jan 15, 2023 and last reviewed on: Jul 18, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】My mother is diagnosed with moderate right hydronephrosis, and proximal hydroureter is seen due to a calculus (1400 HU in attenuation value) in the right upper ureter measuring 13.2 x 7 mm, located approximately 6.5 cm below the pelvic ureteric junction. Two calculi are seen in the mid pole of the right kidney, the largest measuring 3 mm. Tiny calculus measuring 2 mm is seen in the upper pole of the left kidney. She is taking the medications Tenegliptin 20 plus and Metformin 500 mg. Please help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Yash Kathuria

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I understand your concern for your mother.

【14】The stones which are less than 5 mm are not of much concern because they may pass with adequate water intake, that is, 84.5 to 101.4 ounces of water every day. But the stone size of 13 mm has increased pressure in the right side of the kidney, which in the long run may cause irreversible kidney injury. So my suggestion would be this is the clear-cut indication to go to a urologist for stenting and stone removal. As a preventive measure, I suggest taking syrup Potassium citrate two teaspoonfuls daily. Consult a specialist and take medications with their consent.

【15】Hope this helps.

【16】Kind regards.

【17】* * *

【18】* * *

source_info.title: Can a biopsy report confirm Crohn's disease?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can a biopsy report confirm Crohn's disease?
===============================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Utkarsh Sharma**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 14, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I have attached my biopsy report. Can you confirm if I am suffering from Crohn's disease? If not, can the report be wrong?

【9】Thank you.

【10】Answered by Dr. Utkarsh Sharma

【11】#

【12】Hi,

【13】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【14】I understand your concern and will help you regarding it.

【15】I have seen the attached report (the attachment was removed to protect the patient’s identity). The histopathological features described are highly indicative of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or could be Crohn's disease. However, the report should be correlated with radiological findings and clinical findings to arrive at a confirmatory diagnosis. I suggest you undergo a calprotectin stool test, it is a noninvasive test that helps distinguish between IBD, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, and IBS (irritable bowel syndrome). This can help confirm a diagnosis. Treatment is usually aimed at disease remission.

【16】I hope your query was answered.

【17】Take care and stay healthy.

【18】Patient's Query

【19】Hello doctor,

【20】Thank you for the reply.

【21】Can Crohn's disease be confirmed?

【22】Answered by Dr. Utkarsh Sharma

【23】#

【24】Hello,

【25】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【26】I have read your query and I can understand your concern.

【27】Observing the histological features it could be or might not be Crohn's disease. The current available information mostly suggests Crohn's disease. The Crohn's disease can only be confirmed if other tests are performed.

【28】I hope this information will help you.

【29】Thank you.

【30】* * *

source_info.title: I am suffering from chest pain and my chest hurts on smoking. Is this indicative of lung cancer?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I am suffering from chest pain and my chest hurts on smoking. Is this indicative of lung cancer?
===================================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Kaushal Bhavsar**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr.Nithila A

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Aug 16, 2019 and last reviewed on: Jul 06, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am a 28-years-old male with 250 lb. I have little pain in the chest when taking a deep breath, especially in the morning. I do not have a cough at all when I try to cough hard sometimes there is little tiny blood in my saliva, and my mouth tastes bloody. I keep smoking these two weeks a lot which I can see when I smoke a lot my chest hurts, but this blood thing is scaring me that I may have lung cancer. What should I do?

【9】Answered by Dr. Kaushal Bhavsar

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com. I can understand your concern. First of all, do not think directly about lung cancer because the possibility of it is very less. Possibility of other smoking-induced lung diseases like pleurisy , lung infection, bronchitis , etc. is more likely. So please let me know, 1. Since how long do you smoke? 2. How many cigarettes per day? 3. Do you have breathlessness? Please reply to me answers of above-asked questions, so that I can guide you better. I will be happy to help you further.

【13】Patient's Query

【14】Thank you doctor,

【15】I smoke for 10 years, yes I have breathlessness when I smoke a lot. I have a severe anxiety disorder, and one night, I read about lung cancer and how people with lung cancer cough blood. So I start for one week making my self put saliva from my throat sometimes there is tiny little blood, but when I put phlegm from my chest is not blood, but it is brown.

【16】Answered by Dr. Kaushal Bhavsar

【17】#

【18】Hello,

【19】Welcome back to icliniq.com. It will be better if you quit smoking as soon as possible. Have you ever undergone a chest X-ray? Have you ever experienced a PFT (pulmonary function test)? Both these tests are basic tests to diagnose any lung disease. In my opinion, you are having bronchitis. Please reply to me answers of above-asked questions, so that I can guide you better. I will be happy to help you further.

【20】* * *

source_info.title: Is it possible to lead a long and healthy life by continuing Remicade infusions?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Is it possible to lead a long and healthy life by continuing Remicade infusions?
===================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Naval Mendiratta**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jun 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am having ankylosing spondylitis (HLA-B27 Positive) and had six Remicade infusions till now. I responded to the Remicade infusions very well. But after almost three months of every infusion, gradually I received the pain again. I want to know if a person can live a normal life if he continues Remicade infusions. As it is too expensive for me, I will only continue it life-long if there are very high chances of living a normal life with this.

【9】Thank you.

【10】Answered by Dr. Naval Mendiratta

【11】#

【12】Hello,

【13】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【14】Well yes, it does happen sometimes that the disease goes into remission and does not come back again. But when it does, it is something hard to say. I suggest you continue exercises and a short course of painkillers when you get the pain. The point is to prolong the duration of the Remicade. If we can make it once in four to five months then that also would be better. Consult your specialist doctor, discuss with him or her, and take the medicines with their consent. Secondly, Remicade does get ineffective after some time so we need to be sure if it is working well or if we can switch to the other subcutaneous alternatives. Consult your specialist doctor, discuss with him or her, and take the medicines with their consent.

【15】Thank you.

【16】* * *

text.text:
【2】Answered by

===================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Naval Mendiratta**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jun 26, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I am having ankylosing spondylitis (HLA-B27 Positive) and had six Remicade infusions till now. I responded to the Remicade infusions very well. But after almost three months of every infusion, gradually I received the pain again. I want to know if a person can live a normal life if he continues Remicade infusions. As it is too expensive for me, I will only continue it life-long if there are very high chances of living a normal life with this.

【9】Thank you.

【10】Answered by Dr. Naval Mendiratta

【11】#

【12】Hello,

【13】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【14】Well yes, it does happen sometimes that the disease goes into remission and does not come back again. But when it does, it is something hard to say. I suggest you continue exercises and a short course of painkillers when you get the pain. The point is to prolong the duration of the Remicade. If we can make it once in four to five months then that also would be better. Consult your specialist doctor, discuss with him or her, and take the medicines with their consent. Secondly, Remicade does get ineffective after some time so we need to be sure if it is working well or if we can switch to the other subcutaneous alternatives. Consult your specialist doctor, discuss with him or her, and take the medicines with their consent.

【15】Thank you.

source_info.title: My wife has pregnancy symptoms along with heavy bleeding. What does it mean?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. My wife has pregnancy symptoms along with heavy bleeding. What does it mean?
===============================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Dattaprasad Balasaheb Inamdar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 02, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 14, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My wife and I had sex one and a half months ago. We used the withdrawal method for contraception. After four weeks, she showed all the pregnancy symptoms including delayed period. Five weeks after the intercourse, she had heavy bleeding and it continued for four days. I think it was a miscarriage due to her daily walking and excessive work. Then, she took a home pregnancy test, and it shows negative. A week later, she again showed pregnancy symptoms like nausea and abdominal cramps. What does this mean? Is she pregnant? Was the heavy bleeding due to a miscarriage?

【9】Answered by Dr. Dattaprasad Balasaheb Inamdar

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】A negative pregnancy test rules out pregnancy. But, to be safe, you can get a serum beta hCG test done. A negative result will rule out any possibility of pregnancy. All the pregnancy symptoms can occur in the case of pregnancy in tubes, called as ectopic pregnancy, which is quite dangerous. So do get a blood test done and if positive, she needs an ultrasound immediately, to rule out ectopic pregnancy. In the case of a negative result, the cause of the symptoms can be a stomach infection. If the infection is mild, the symptoms should subside in two to three days. In the case of a severe infection where symptoms are intolerable, she needs to consult a doctor.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: What can cause genital numbness?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What can cause genital numbness?
===================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Chandan Mohanty**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Dec 07, 2017 and last reviewed on: Jul 27, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I have been riding my bike a lot more recently and now I noticed that I am having numbness within the perineal region including scrotum and penile area. I have stopped riding since the onset of symptoms and it has been over a week now. Should these symptoms resolve with time if I quit riding? Please suggest.

【9】Answered by Dr. Chandan Mohanty

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com. The two most common causes of perineal or genital numbness is compression of the nerves in your spine (called as cauda equina) or compression of the nerves in the perineum itself. Only sensory loss is uncommon but still possible in cauda equina syndrome (CES), since it is more commonly associated with other symptoms. Compression of nerve in the perineum typically occurs in cyclists. I will suggest you to go to the closest ER (emergency room) urgently. You need to be evaluated to reach the correct diagnosis. They may also order an magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for you to identify the exact site of nerve compression since the treatment varies as per the site of compression. Delay in treatment may make the symptoms irreversible.

【13】Patient's Query

【14】Hello doctor,

【15】What is the treatment for perineal nerve compression most often? Are nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and rest the treatment? Please guide.

【16】Answered by Dr. Chandan Mohanty

【17】#

【18】Hi,

【19】Welcome back to icliniq.com. Yes. You are right. NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) and rest are the main treatment given for perineal nerve compression. In addition the following need to be done. 1. Use of ring cushion to sit. 2. Avoid straining during micturition and emptying your bowels. Wish you a speedy recovery.

【20】* * *

source_info.title: How safe is it to get anesthesia before getting a polyp removed?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. How safe is it to get anesthesia before getting a polyp removed?
===================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Kiran Kumar Kolla Gopalkrishna**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jan 30, 2023 and last reviewed on: Feb 06, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I am having a polyp removed, and they will be administering Propofol. I am terrified of the anesthesia. I keep reading that it is a respiratory depressant. I am going to take Xanax beforehand. I want to know how safe it is.

【9】Answered by Dr. Kiran Kumar Kolla Gopalkrishna

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I read your query and can understand your concern.

【14】It is called general anesthesia . Propofol is an intravenous, very short-acting anesthetic. The anesthetist will control your breathing. It is a routine procedure.

【15】You can take Xanax. It will calm and relax you.

【16】Where is the polyp, you have yet to mention? If they are using Propofol , it will be a short procedure.

【17】Please do not worry.

【18】Hope this helps.

【19】Thank you and take care.

【20】Patient's Query

【21】Hi doctor,

【22】Thank you for your reply.

【23】The polyp is in my uterus and causes bleeding every day. I am very grateful for your reassurance.

【24】Answered by Dr. Kiran Kumar Kolla Gopalkrishna

【25】#

【26】Hi,

【27】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【28】I read your query and can understand your concern.

【29】Do not worry, it will take a maximum of one hour. As you are overweight, they will insert a small tube-like thing when you happily sleep under anesthesia. You will not even know when it is inserted or removed. You may have a scratchy feeling after surgery, and you will be given opioids for pain.

【30】Now general anesthesia is advanced and safe. Short acting medications and safe anesthetics are available.

【31】Surgery is a minor one. So, do not worry and do not take any stimulants, and sleep well.

【32】Please do reply to me when the surgery is done.

【33】Hope this helps.

【34】Thank you and take care.

【35】* * *

【1】Q. How safe is it to get anesthesia before getting a polyp removed?
===================================================================

【2】<mark>Answered by

【3】Dr. Kiran Kumar Kolla Gopalkrishna

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】This is a premium question & answer published on Jan 30, 2023 and last reviewed on: Feb 06, 2023

【6】Patient’s Query</mark>nt's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I am having a polyp removed, and they will be administering Propofol. I am terrified of the anesthesia. I keep reading that it is a respiratory depressant. I am going to take Xanax beforehand. I want to know how safe it is.

【9】Answered by Dr. Kiran Kumar Kolla Gopalkrishna

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I read your query and can understand your concern.

【14】It is called general anesthesia . Propofol is an intravenous, very short-acting anesthetic. The anesthetist will control your breathing. It is a routine procedure.

【15】You can take Xanax. It will calm and relax you.

【16】Where is the polyp, you have yet to mention? If they are using Propofol , it will be a short procedure.

【17】Please do not worry.

【18】Hope this helps.

【19】Thank you and take care.

【20】Patient's Query

【21】Hi doctor,

【22】Thank you for your reply.

【23】The polyp is in my uterus and causes bleeding every day. I am very grateful for your reassurance.

【24】Answered by Dr. Kiran Kumar Kolla Gopalkrishna

【25】#

【26】Hi,

【27】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【28】I read your query and can understand your concern.

【29】Do not worry, it will take a maximum of one hour. As you are overweight, they will insert a small tube-like thing when you happily sleep under anesthesia. You will not even know when it is inserted or removed. You may have a scratchy feeling after surgery, and you will be given opioids for pain.

【30】Now general anesthesia is advanced and safe. Short acting medications and safe anesthetics are available.

【31】Surgery is a minor one. So, do not worry and do not take any stimulants, and sleep well.

【32】Please do reply to me when the surgery is done.

【33】Hope this helps.

【34】Thank you and take care.

【35】* * *

source_info.title: Can diabetic medicine cause rise in creatinine level?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. Can diabetic medicine cause rise in creatinine level?
========================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Mhetras Ganesh Nagesh**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on May 11, 2018 and last reviewed on: Jul 13, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】My aunt is 44 years old. Her reports are plasma glucose is 119 mg/dL, blood urea is 61 mg/dL and serum creatinine is 3.0 mg/dL. Doctor has told that, the medicine she has been taking for sugar is affecting her kidney. Please provide some advice.

【9】Thank you.

【10】Answered by Dr. Mhetras Ganesh Nagesh

【11】#

【12】Hi,

【13】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【14】I would like to know whether your aunt is a long-standing diabetes patient. Diabetes mellitus is a condition where ones sugar level is higher than normal and need to take medicines to bring to normalcy. If she has been a long-standing diabetes patient kidneys can get affected by diabetes itself. When was first time creatinine report abnormality detected? But, I will need more details before I give you any meaningful advice. Do you have a past history of diabetes or hypertension? If any, please let me know their duration. Kindly get a routine urine examination, ultrasound of kidneys as well as complete blood count.

【15】Thank you.

【16】* * *

【17】**The Probable causes:**  

【18】Diabetes Mellitus.

【19】**Investigations to be done:**  

【20】1\. Urine routine examination.  
  
2\. Ultrasound kidneys.  
  
3\. Eye checkup for diabetic retinopathy

【21】Patient's Query

【22】Hello doctor,

【23】She has been taking medicine for blood sugar for 12 years and feels that, medicine has affected her kidney. Hence, she has started taking low dose insulin from yesterday. I have sent you more detailed report.

【24】Please guide.

【25】Thank you.

【26】Answered by Dr. Mhetras Ganesh Nagesh

【27】#

【28】Hello,

【29】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【30】After reviewing all her reports ( _attachments removed to protect patient identity_ ) and additional information, following inference can be made. Diabetes is the most common cause of chronic kidney disease nowadays. CKD is a disease where, kidneys functional ability is reduced and reflected as elevated creatinine. In her case, the cause is diabetes. There are stages of CKD from 1 to 5 depending upon level of creatinine. Stage 1 is earliest while in stage 5 patient may need dialysis. Due to reduced kidney functions, kidneys cannot degrade anti-diabetic tablets, so insulin is preferred.

【31】Diet modifications:

【32】1\. She needs to be on specialized diet called renal diet. It is essentially protein restricted diet,so as to slow down further rise in creatinine.

【33】2\. Avoid medicines which are likely to affect kidneys adversely like painkillers and certain antibiotics like Aminoglycosides.

【34】3\. Keep blood pressure under control. Certain other medications are recommended to slow down further progression of this CKD.

【35】Please consult nearby nephrologist (kidney specialist) for further physical evaluation and individualized treatment plan.

【36】Thank you.

【37】* * *

【38】**The Probable causes:**  

【39】Diabetes.

【40】**Investigations to be done:**  

【41】Get these investigations done.  
  
Serum calcium, phosphorus, serum bicarbonate and hemogram.

【42】**Probable diagnosis:**  

【43】Chronic kidney disease (CKD) due to diabetic nephropathy.

【44】**Treatment plan:**  

【45】1\. Renal diet.  
  
2\. Medicines.  
  
3\. Counseling.

【46】* * *

source_info.title: What are the probable causes of inadequate anesthetic effect on the lower jaw?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What are the probable causes of inadequate anesthetic effect on the lower jaw?
=================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Purva Jingar**

【4】and medically reviewed by iCliniq medical review team.

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 16, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】When it comes to having a tooth extracted, I often experience difficulty getting numb in my lower jaw. Despite getting the maximum dose of anesthesia, there have been incidences where I do not get enough numbness, especially in my lower jaw. In such circumstances, what should be the course of my action? Should I go ahead with the procedure even if my lower jaw is not fully numb, or should I request my dentist to reschedule the treatment? I am concerned about if my asking for reschedule would irritate the dentist and if rescheduling would be an inconvenience to my dentist. Kindly help.

【9】Answered by Dr. Purva Jingar

【10】#

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】I have read your query and understood your concern. There can be many reasons for not having enough numbness in your lower jaw. These include increasing age, smoking, drinking alcohol, diabetes, or an abscess in the tooth that has to be extracted. With regard to this, I suggest that if you are a smoker, then quit as soon as possible. If you have diabetes, inform the doctor and take medication prior to the treatment to control it. If you have an abscess in the tooth to be extracted, it may hinder the anesthesia from working effectively in that specific area. In such cases, it is important to cooperate with the doctor. I recommend asking the doctor to use liquid nitrogen or anesthesia sprays. After the tooth extraction, take the prescribed painkiller one hour after the extraction and carefully follow the dentist's instructions.

【14】* * *

【15】**The Probable causes:**  

【16】The probable causes can be smoking, drinking, diabetes, aging, or an abscess in the tooth.

【17】**Investigations to be done:**  

【18】Investigations to be done include an X-ray of the tooth to be extracted.

【19】**Differential diagnosis:**  

【20】Differential diagnoses include periapical abscess, drinking habits, and facial paralysis.

【21】**Probable diagnosis:**  

【22】The probable diagnosis is a periapical abscess.

【23】**Treatment plan:**  

【24】The treatment plan includes following the instructions given after extraction and using painkillers after an hour of extraction.

【25】**Preventive measures:**  

【26】Preventive measures include not spitting after extraction, avoiding smoking or drinking, consuming soft semi-solid food, and drinking cold water or eating ice cream after an hour of extraction.

【27】**Regarding follow up:**  

【28】Regarding follow-up, visit the dentist after seven days of extraction.

【29】* * *

【11】Hello,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【24】The treatment plan includes following the instructions given after extraction and using painkillers after an hour of extraction.

【26】Preventive measures include not spitting after extraction, avoiding smoking or drinking, consuming soft semi-solid food, and drinking cold water or eating ice cream after an hour of extraction.

【28】Regarding follow-up, visit the dentist after seven days of extraction.

source_info.text:
【0】I have swelling even after aspiration of fluid from the scrotum after hydrocelectomy. Why? 
Listen

【1】Q. I have swelling even after aspiration of fluid from the scrotum after hydrocelectomy. Why?
=============================================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Samer Sameer Juma Ali Altawil**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Sushrutha Muralidharan

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jul 13, 2021_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】Thirty days ago, I had a double hydrocelectomy. After surgery, there was a lot of swelling, which was slow to do down, and then suddenly, three weeks out, it quickly went up. Following an ultrasound, my scrotum was aspirated, draining off 520 ml of fluid. Two days later, it is once again very swollen. What needs to be done now? Kindly help me.

【9】Answered by Dr. Samer Sameer Juma Ali Altawil

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Swelling and fluid indicate fluid leaking from the tummy down through the inguinal canal to the scrotum. Hydrocele can be non-communicating, which can be treated by classical hydrocelectomy , but the communicating type should have ligation of the patent vaginalis at the inguinal canal.

【14】In your case, I think the processus vaginalis are not lighted, and fluid accumulates in the scrotum again. Treatment is by exploring both inguinal canals and ligation of processus vaginalis.

【15】If you have any more queries, please do not hesitate to ask.

【16】Patient's Query

【17】Hi doctor,

【18】Does this involve surgery? Kindly give your opinion.

【19】Answered by Dr. Samer Sameer Juma Ali Altawil

【20】#

【21】Hi,

【22】Welcome back to icliniq.com.

【23】Yes, revision needs surgery on both inguinal areas to separate the processus vaginalis from the spermatic cord and ligate it. I hope this was helpful.

【24】* * *

source_info.title: What are the lifestyle changes to be followed to get cured from fatty liver?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. What are the lifestyle changes to be followed to get cured from fatty liver?
===============================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Muhammad Zohaib Siddiq**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. K Shobana

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Jan 31, 2021 and last reviewed on: Jul 10, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hi doctor,

【8】I have a grade 2 fatty liver with mild hepatomegaly. I have tightness in the right side of the abdomen. I have fatigue and lethargy after doing physical exercise. I feel fine when I am not exerting myself. I have mild acid reflux when I eat the wrong foods. What to do?

【9】Answered by Dr. Muhammad Zohaib Siddiq

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com.

【13】Fatty liver is caused due to alcohol consumption. In people who do not drink alcohol, fatty liver is called nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). It is caused due to obesity, lack of exercise, diabetes, insulin resistance, excessive belly fat, and excessive intake of refined sugars and fats. In many cases, NAFLD can regress back if the cause is treated. In your case, it caused due to obesity. Try to do exercise, reduce weight slowly and cut refined sugars and fatty meals. Check your fasting and random blood sugar. If it is normal, then it is fine. If it is on the borderline, then you need to do a glucose tolerance test. Also, do liver function tests to rule out the elements of hepatitis. NAFLD can progress to nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and this progresses to cirrhosis. Reduce your weight and modify your lifestyle including diet. Take a mediterranean diet. Fatty liver occurs commonly in south asians due to their genes. Do not worry and follow these modifications.

【14】* * *

source_info.title: I have a cold two months after COVID. Is it due to COVID or allergic asthma?
source_info.text:
【0】Listen

【1】Q. I have a cold two months after COVID. Is it due to COVID or allergic asthma?
===============================================================================

【2】Answered by

【3】**Dr. Muhammad Zubayer Alam**

【4】and medically reviewed by Dr. Sushrutha Muralidharan

【5】_This is a **premium question & answer** published on Sep 09, 2021 and last reviewed on: Jul 17, 2023_

【6】Patient's Query

【7】Hello doctor,

【8】I had COVID on the seventh two months ago, and the first negative report came on the fourteenth two months ago. Now I am recovering from COVID. However, today I had a cold, sneezing, and headache as I went outside in hot weather. I had the same problem of getting cold, sneezing, and headaches earlier, particularly when I was exposed to too hot or too cold weather. Sometimes I get a fever and cough too. This happens in a change of weather too. The doctor suggested I have allergic asthma. Most of the time, when I have a cold or cough, some wheezing is also there. I went for an allergic test around four to five years ago and found allergic to dust, molds, smells, and cockroach. Currently, I am taking Foracort 200 and Montair-LC. Today again, when I went outside having hot exposure, I got cold, sneezing, and headache. Please suggest if I have asthma. If yes, how to get rid of this cold with hot exposure. Or is it an after COVID effect? Kindly give your opinion.

【9】Answered by Dr. Muhammad Zubayer Alam

【10】#

【11】Hi,

【12】Welcome to icliniq.com. I can understand your concern. According to your statement, you have been suffering from allergic rhinitis or pre-asthmatic status. Allergic rhinitis is associated with symptoms that can mainly affect your nose. These symptoms may result from when you breathe in something you are allergic to, like dust, smoke, dander, molds, perfumes, pollen, mites, spores, etc. Allergic rhinitis is the inflammation of the nasal membranes characterized by sneezing, nasal congestion, nasal irritation, runny nose, coughing, etc. Again, climate changes, too hot weather, or too cold weather may trigger allergic rhinitis. Patients with allergic rhinitis are prone to develop sinus headaches characterized by soreness behind their cheekbones and forehead. Wearing a face mask, stay away from the triggering factors like dust, smoke, dander, or pollen, during climate changing take antihistamines like Fexofenadine, using intranasal corticosteroids, leukotriene receptor antagonists like Montelukast, oral steroids, etc., may help you to relieve from allergic rhinitis or pre-asthmatic status. Your present and history suggest that you are most probably suffering from allergic rhinitis now, rather than COVID-19 infection . For your headache, you can take Acetaminophen or Paracetamol. I hope this was helpful.

【13】* * *

===================================================================

【2】Answered by
